Event: `3046b9a222071f76f0eaa8f896bb10eb` · 2026-09-23T22:34:06Z

> Owner decision needed on question 166 (docs/QUESTIONS.md): the one-slice wakeup promise versus the single stride queue (ASTRA D3). K5 is blocked on this; G1 cannot close without it.
> 
> THE GAP. Answer 103 (archive 2026-09-22) replaced the `first` flag with one stride queue for every budget and stated as its cost: "a driver woken by an interrupt re-enters at the minimum pass, so it runs within about one SLICE". KERNEL-SPEC R12, RESOURCES.md (Scheduling, Attack tests) and BUILD-PLAN WP-K5 acceptance all repeat that as a bound. It does not follow from the specified mechanism. R12 wakes at max(own pass, current minimum) and says nothing about ties or when preemption happens. A woken driver therefore waits for the remainder of the running slice plus one full SLICE for every runnable budget ranked ahead of it at an equal pass, and it keeps any larger pass it retained. No unconditional next-turn bound exists, and a large weight does not create one. Nothing has been measured. Either the claim is weakened or the scheduler is changed; an editor may not choose.
> 
> RECOMMENDATION (A): keep answer 103's mechanism, withdraw the universal one-slice claim, replace it with a specified tie rule and a measured target.
> - KERNEL-SPEC R12: delete the sentence "Because a waking budget re-enters at the current minimum pass, a driver woken by an interrupt runs within about one SLICE" and the open-qualification paragraph. Add: a waking budget is ranked ahead of already-queued budgets with an equal pass (deterministic tie handling, wake-first); preemption happens at slice end or at a deadline, never on wake alone; wakeup is prompt but not bounded, and no deadline follows from weight. Single queue, actual-runtime charging and the max wake rule are unchanged.
> - RESOURCES.md: remove the two open-166 paragraphs and the "Unresolved latency claim" bullet; state the wake rule as prompt-not-bounded with the tie rule; replace the attack-test bullet "a driver woken by an interrupt runs within about one SLICE while user budgets spin" with a measured responsiveness target under a named workload (N spinning user budgets at manifest user weight, one driver and the steward at manifest weights) that records weights, runnable budgets, prior passes, wake latency and lease-termination latency. Share, fairness and human-control text stay.
> - BUILD-PLAN WP-K5: replace the bold one-SLICE acceptance bullet with: deterministic tie handling implemented and tested; real-boot acceptance under the named workload reports the measured wake and lease-termination latencies with the recorded inputs; WP-K5 proposes the numeric target with its evidence and a package reviewer accepts it. Remove the design-gate line. Answer 103's "stated cost" wording is superseded by the new entry; TENETS' reference to open 166 is removed editorially.
> - Why: it preserves the accepted no-priority design, makes the guarantee honest and testable, and costs nothing in mechanism. Residual: human control (TENETS guarantee 3) then rests on a measured steward latency, not a proven bound.
> 
> ALTERNATIVE (B): keep a hard "within one SLICE" requirement and change the scheduler to establish it.
> - KERNEL-SPEC R12 gains a wake rule that guarantees the next turn (for example: a budget woken by an interrupt, or any budget above a weight threshold, is placed at the queue head with a rate limit per period), plus an explicit rule against sleeping to gain priority.
> - RESOURCES.md states the load assumptions under which the bound holds and the proof sketch; the attack-test bullet stays as a bound.
> - WP-K5 acceptance keeps the one-SLICE bullet and adds attack cases for sleep-wake gaming and starvation by several head-jumping budgets; a defensive review of the rule precedes implementation.
> - Cost: this reintroduces a form of the priority tier answer 103 removed, needs a new proof under stated assumptions, and delays K5 by that design and review.
> 
> MINOR VARIANT (A without a measured target): retain the qualification and let K5 ship with no latency claim at all. Not recommended: the steward's responsiveness underwrites lease termination, so some recorded evidence is needed.
> 
> Please answer A, B, or a variation with any change you want to the tie rule, the workload or the numeric target. Only your reply authorizes the edits; I will then record the decision in ANSWERS.md as a revision of 103, apply it to R12, RESOURCES.md and WP-K5, and return the thread to the orchestrator with decision references.

## G1 · G1-write-without-read — Should set_flags and process_map refuse write-without-read pages, like map_anon?

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 7

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

Decision references: docs/KERNEL-SPEC.md: R11 and the map_anon/set_flags/process_map Errors rows (Architect, settled rule), commit cf5465b85

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `619e54ab8bed964ebab3fbaac921673d` · 2026-09-24T05:37:05Z

> G1 red team (assignment 4c1ad5c9) found that the kernel installs the reserved RISC-V encoding W-without-R through two runtime paths: set_flags(page, W) on a caller's own R|W page (kernel/src/mem.rs:1221-1241 -> arch/riscv/mem.rs:752, check_permissions rejects only empty and W|X), and process_map(child, ..., W) (kernel/src/process.rs:351-355). map_anon rejects W-without-R (mem.rs:1139-1143), matching its KERNEL-SPEC Errors row; the set_flags and process_map rows do not, and R11 does not forbid it. Consequence today: none within spec order, because read_record checks readable first. But user_frame's writable check does not imply readable, so any future single-pass record check would read a record the user cannot. Question: should the set_flags and process_map rows gain 'W without R' like map_anon, or should the spec state the encoding is allowed and unreadable? Red team recommends also requiring R whenever user_frame checks W. Nonblocking for G1; to be delivered to the Architect after the wash rebuild.

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `8006ac1eb498f4e53cac475d4f967db3` · 2026-09-24T05:54:41Z

> Spec question from the G1 red team (clear review debt before the scheduler work), nonblocking; full evidence is in the thread's opening event. The kernel installs the reserved RISC-V W-without-R encoding through set_flags(page, W) and process_map(child, ..., W). map_anon refuses it and its KERNEL-SPEC Errors row says so; the set_flags and process_map rows do not, and R11 is silent. Should those rows gain "W without R" like map_anon, or should the spec state the encoding is allowed and unreadable? Give your recommendation and alternatives. If it is a genuine owner choice, raise a decision_request on this thread; otherwise cite the settled rule. Reply on this thread.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `1d408d8be73db0f340cac84cf5c98715` · 2026-09-24T05:57:59Z

> Settled rule, not an owner choice: no user mapping is ever writable without being readable, and every call that installs or changes permissions refuses W-without-R with InvalidArgument. No decision_request raised.
> 
> WHY IT IS SETTLED
> - The executable model, the conformance oracle, already applies one check_flags (flags 0, or W without R -> InvalidArgument) to map_anon, set_flags AND process_map (model/src/kernel.rs:544-550, called at 2369, 2389 and 2552). The spec's map_anon row documented it; the set_flags and process_map rows merely omitted it. The kernel accepting W-only in set_flags (kernel/src/mem.rs:1221-1241 via arch check_permissions) and process_map (kernel/src/process.rs:351-357) is therefore a kernel/model conformance gap, a finding, not a spec option.
> - TENETS 4 (ratified RISC-V specifications only) and "fail closed": the privileged architecture's PTE permission table marks XWR = 010 and 110 "reserved for future use", so installing it is not a defined, unreadable page; it is an unspecified encoding whose behaviour the ISA does not promise. The alternative "allowed and unreadable" would need a tenet amendment and cannot be specified against the ratified ISA, so it is not a live alternative.
> - R11 is the one statement of memory invariants; W^X was there and this sibling rule belongs beside it.
> 
> APPLIED (editorial consolidation under the QA protocol; no new approval needed; docs/KERNEL-SPEC.md only, unstaged, uncommitted):
> - R11 now reads: no mapping is writable and executable, and none is writable without being readable; the privileged architecture reserves that encoding, so map_anon, set_flags and process_map refuse it with InvalidArgument, and a writable user page is always readable.
> - Errors table: set_flags row now "InvalidArgument (range; flags 0, or W without R; a page not the caller's own mapping)"; process_map row now "... flags 0, or W without R ...". map_anon row unchanged. Check order unchanged (flags are checked where each row already lists "flags").
> 
> ALTERNATIVE considered and rejected: decode-time refusal of W-without-R (like W+X in libs/sys MemFlags::from_bits). Not chosen because W+X is refused at decode by an already-approved rule (ABI, Decoding) and changing the wire-level decoder for every caller is a bigger, unapproved change; the row-level kernel check matches the model exactly and is enough. If the orchestrator wants decode-time refusal as well, that is a small follow-on spec change I can make, but it is not required for consistency.
> 
> IMPLEMENTATION FOLLOW-UPS (not architect work; suggest folding into G1's review-debt fixes or K5's kernel-writer slot):
> 1. Kernel: refuse W-without-R in set_flags and process_map, matching map_anon. Simplest single place: arch check_permissions (kernel/src/arch/riscv/mem.rs:161) gains the readable requirement, since map_anon's map_run, set_flags and process_map all reach it; keep map_anon's explicit row check so neither rests on the other (the existing pattern for W+X).
> 2. Red team's user_frame point (arch/riscv/mem.rs:728-739): with the invariant in force, a writable user PTE is always readable, so a single-pass "writable" record check is sound. A debug assertion that W implies R in user_frame is cheap defence in depth; no spec change.
> 3. Tests: bench attack cases that set_flags(page, W) and process_map(child, ..., W) return InvalidArgument and leave the mapping/permissions unchanged; a model mutation "R11 set_flags/process_map allow W without R" alongside the existing R11SetFlagsAllowsWx so the checker proves the model's rule bites.
> 
> No other document references this rule. Returning the thread to the orchestrator; resolution needs the kernel fix and tests as evidence.

Event: `622a5adf7a436bd7bac8701bf93709e6` · 2026-09-24T07:03:08Z

> 
> Recommendation: add to the `startup` message (opcode 1), after `argv`:
> - `image_addr: u64` — the first byte of the ELF image, which the parent mapped read-write into the child's own address space (`process_map`), page-aligned. 0 means "no image named" (a process started directly at its own entry, not through the stub — e.g. the boot bundle's initial processes, or a launcher that already knows its child's entry).
> - `image_len: u64` — the exact byte length of the image (not rounded to pages); bytes in the image's last page past this length are not part of it. Must be 0 iff `image_addr` is 0.
> 
> Why `u64` for both, not `u32`: WIRE.md's convention for addresses/lengths that must be the same shape on both widths (cf. `read`'s `block: u64` in the example table); an rv64 address does not fit `u32`.
> 
> Why paired presence rather than a separate boolean: mirrors `handle_count`/`handles` and keeps the block one shape for every process, stub-launched or not; `redoubt-rt`'s startup reader treats `(0, 0)` as "no image" and anything else as a candidate the stub validates (page-aligned `image_addr`, `image_addr + image_len` does not overflow). It cannot check the range lies inside what the parent actually mapped — a parent that lies can only fault its own child (PACKAGES.md, "A malicious ELF can at most compromise the process it was going to become").
> 
> Separately, and not blocking this question: PACKAGES.md says the stub is mapped "at a fixed address, the same for everyone." I plan to treat that address as an implementation constant in a small shared crate both the stub and its launchers (`init`, the steward) import, not a spec table entry, since `process_map`'s destination address is caller-chosen (KERNEL-SPEC.md) and nothing else needs to know the value. Flag if you'd rather this live in INIT.md instead.

## R2 · R2-stub-self-map — No syscall lets a running process map memory at an address it chooses, within itself

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 15

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

Decision references: docs/ANSWERS.md: answer 172, docs/KERNEL-SPEC.md: R11; System calls (map_fixed); Errors (map_fixed), docs/PACKAGES.md: Launching a process, step 5

### Implementer · Question

Event: `ade100ae742b51f05d21d6648680e5be` · 2026-09-24T07:10:22Z

> Blocking gap found while building the stub's ELF-mapping half (WP-R2): I can't find a syscall that lets an already-started process map memory at an address *it chooses* within itself.
> 
> PACKAGES.md step 5: "The stub, running inside the new process's own budget, parses the ELF from memory, maps its segments... at their vaddr." But KERNEL-SPEC.md's table has only:
> - `map_anon(len, flags) -> addr`: the **kernel** chooses the address ("nothing may depend on them").
> - `process_map(h(process), src, dst, len, flags)`: caller-chosen `dst`, but only into a process that is **not started** (`NotPermitted` otherwise) — and the stub *is* that process, already started when it runs.
> - `set_flags`/`unmap`: act on memory already mapped, not new mappings.
> 
> Redoubt's native binaries are non-PIE, fixed-address statics (confirmed by `tests/programs/src/spawn.rs`'s doc comment: "Identical addresses mean the copy's code... resolve as they do here" — it relies on placing a copy at the *same* absolute address, not a computed slide). So the stub cannot silently reinterpret an ELF's `p_vaddr` as PIE-relative to wherever `map_anon` happens to land; that would be guessing at a load convention the design never stated, and would diverge from how every other Redoubt binary is built and linked today.
> 
> Options, for you to pick (I have not implemented any of these):
> 1. A new syscall, e.g. `map_fixed(addr, len, flags) -> ()`, letting a process map its own zeroed pages at an address of its own choosing (only within its own budget/address space, same admission and W^X rules as `map_anon`/`set_flags`). This is the smallest addition and the one PACKAGES.md's wording ("maps its segments") seems to assume.
> 2. The parent maps the segments instead, before `process_start`, via `process_map` (which *can* target a caller-chosen `dst` on an unstarted process) — but then the stub isn't the one parsing+mapping the ELF, contradicting PACKAGES.md step 5 and R2's whole reason to exist (the parent would have to parse the ELF to know where the segments go, which is exactly what R2 exists to avoid: "init and the steward copy bytes; they never parse an ELF").
> 3. Something else I haven't considered.
> 
> This blocks only the actual on-target mapping call; I can keep building and host-testing everything else (ELF parsing, segment bounds-checking, the crate/build skeleton) meanwhile. Recommend (1): smallest kernel change, keeps the stub the sole ELF parser, and K5 is already the resident kernel writer this milestone.

Flags follow `map_anon`'s rules (not 0, not W+X, not W without R); other error is `OutOfMemory`. `map_anon` and its existing callers stay unchanged. It is a small kernel package with attack cases.
> 
> Alternatives:
> A) Add an `addr` argument to `map_anon` (0 means the kernel chooses). This keeps one allocation call but changes the ABI for every existing caller.
> B) No kernel change: build every native program as a static PIE and have the stub apply relocations wherever `map_anon` lands. The stub gets a relocator, every program's build and the boot loader's `init` path change, and the TCB stays the same size.
> (Rejected: the parent maps the segments before start. That makes init and the steward parse ELFs, which PACKAGES.md forbids.)

## K5a · K5a-addr0 — Lower bound of user space: may map_fixed (or any user address) be 0?

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 4

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `03562f219681e41a08f923e344193af6` · 2026-09-24T08:13:26Z

> K5a (map_fixed, answer 172) found a kernel/model divergence the spec does not settle. KERNEL-SPEC never states a lower bound for "user space". The kernel's MemoryManager::user_range (kernel/src/mem.rs) accepts addr 0; the executable model's user_range refuses it (model/src/kernel.rs: USER_BASE = PAGE_SIZE). map_fixed is the first call where the caller picks an address in its own space, so map_fixed(0, PAGE, RW) is now reachable: the kernel would map page 0, the model refuses it.
> Question: must user space exclude page 0 (null-page guard, so the kernel's user_range gains a floor for every call that takes a user address), or should the model drop USER_BASE to match the kernel? Please settle from existing rules if any (R11, MEMORY-LAYOUT), else request an owner decision with a recommendation. Either answer changes only the rule both sides enforce and an addr-0 attack case in K5a. Reply on this thread to the orchestrator; K5a's implementer is paused awaiting plan approval.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `db673eabf4ddc5543745ef3b20f2a893` · 2026-09-24T08:19:23Z

> Settled by existing rules; no owner decision needed. Page 0 is in user space; the model changes to match the kernel.
> 
> Why: MEMORY-LAYOUT owns the address-space split. Its Userspace row says only "below 0x40_0000_0000" (Sv39) / "below 0x8000_0000" (Sv32), with no lower bound. KERNEL-SPEC's "in user space" (map_fixed row; Errors) points to that definition. R11 and answer 172 add no floor. The kernel's user_range (mem.rs:1117) already follows the spec, and so does process_map's dst check (process.rs:405). model/src/kernel.rs USER_BASE = PAGE_SIZE is a rule that exists only in the model, with no approval behind it, so it's a model defect, not a spec gap. Adding a null-page floor would change frozen v4 (TENETS: it needs an ANSWERS entry). I don't recommend one: sstatus.SUM stays clear, so the kernel never dereferences user pointers, and the usual kernel null-dereference exploit can't happen. A mapped page 0 only affects the process that mapped it or its parent (process_map).
> 
> Spec edit (editorial, no approval needed): MEMORY-LAYOUT.md, Decision 2 paragraph, now says outright that user space starts at 0 on both widths and that map_fixed/process_map/unmap/set_flags accept page 0, with the SUM reason. It's uncommitted in the main tree for you to commit.
>

Invert the addr-0 case: map_fixed(0, PAGE, RW) succeeds in both kernel and model, and a second map_fixed(0, PAGE, RW) fails with InvalidArgument (overlap). Keep the refusal cases from answer 172 (outside user space: end > USER_AREA_END, overflow on addr+len). Returning to the orchestrator to hand back to the K5a implementer. A range that both overlaps a mapping and exceeds the budget must return InvalidArgument (Errors row: range before OutOfMemory), and that variant would return OutOfMemory. Fix, same error order and bounded: (i) an occupancy walk that skips absent subtrees. When the level-L table is missing, jump to the next level-L boundary (Sv39: 1 GiB or 2 MiB; Sv32: 4 MiB). The cost is at most the root entries plus 512 x the tables present in the range, and those tables are charged to the caller. This is a new arch helper, e.g. range_available_in, so the plan's 'no new function' changes. (ii) Split the charge check the way the row reads: npages > free is OutOfMemory (pages), then npages + tables_needed > free is OutOfMemory (page tables). tables_needed then walks at most free_pages pages. Model: use p.space.range(first..first+n).next().is_none() rather than a loop over each vpn.

> Confirmed:
> (i) range_available_in skips absent subtrees correctly on Sv39 and Sv32. User space has no superpage leaves, so a missing child really does mean an empty range. The work is bounded by the root entries spanned plus the tables present in the range, which the caller pays for.

The pages check caps tables_needed's work at the caller's free_pages, so a huge len now returns after a cheap root skip.
> (iii) The model and kernel give the same result at every step. decode_flags matches the kernel's decode (unknown bits, W+X). check_flags matches the kernel's three-way check; its W+X arm can't be reached after decode. The model's single n+tables charge and the kernel's two steps both return OutOfMemory. The overlap check agrees, because the model keeps LentIn and LentOut pages in p.space. Legacy reservations, stub, startup and stack pages are kernel-only, as the plan says.
> (iv) The W+X check runs before the charge, and the expect text names the assumption that budgets are backed by RAM.

The raw generator's process_map dst can already put a child mapping near USER_TOP. There the fallback turns a model OutOfMemory into success, which is the kernel's answer. So a seeded test could change result, and if one does, the new result is correct. The same fix also closes this divergence, which predates map_fixed.
> N2 (P3), model map_fixed: return OutOfMemory when n > free before calling tables_needed. Without that, the hostile trace map_fixed(0, USER_TOP) puts 2^26 vpns through tables_needed's BTreeSet, and hostile replays must finish (hostile_traces_are_refused_cleanly). map_fresh already has the same cost, so fixing it there is optional.
> N3 (P3), range_available_in: fail closed when an entry above the leaf level is non-empty but not a table (child None and !is_empty) instead of skipping it. That can't happen today. If a user superpage ever existed, though, skipping would call the range free, and prepare_map's walk would then hit BadAddress under .expect. Also compute the jump as min((a | (span-1)) + 1, end), which can't wrap on either width because end <= USER_AREA_END. Sv32 tables have 1024 entries, not 512; that only affects the wording of the cost claim.

Event: `d0ae2a9e7031a9804ce4872e0832eed1` · 2026-09-24T15:12:49Z

> K5a review round 1 (defensive), d7b3cc21f against 06b2affe3. Merge verdict: BLOCK, on test coverage only. The kernel and model code is correct; the boot test does not yet cover plan v2's list.
> 
> Ran: ./test --arch rv64 map-fixed-attack PASS. REDOUBT_MODEL_MUTATIONS=R11MapFixedSkipsOverlap mutations_are_caught: caught by kernel_sequence seed 1 ('R6: frame 2 is charged to 7 but mapped nowhere'). model --test map_fixed_contracts: 8/8 pass.
> 
> Code confirmed:
> - kernel/src/mem.rs:1253-1302: the order is user_range, overlap, flags (three-way, W+X included), pages, pages+tables, matching the Errors row. Nothing is charged or allocated before the last check.
> - The .expects after the charge can't be reached: prepare_map's is_occupied is weaker than range_available_in's !is_empty; flags are checked; tables were counted; alloc_page's physical-RAM assumption is named, as in process_map.
> - range_available_in / subtree_occupied (arch/riscv/mem.rs:651-697): the jump is clamped to end. wrapping_add can reach 0 only at the top of the address space, and end <= USER_AREA_END (2^38 on rv64, 2^31 on rv32) keeps it unreachable. A non-table entry above the leaf level fails closed (child() is is_table()). Level spans come from leaf_size and vpn, so 1024 entries on Sv32 and 512 on Sv39 are right.
> - The model's order (model/src/kernel.rs map_fixed) gives the same result as the kernel at every step.
> - The saturating_sub in alloc_va's fallback hides nothing. p.space.range is ascending and cursor = max(cursor, v+1), so v >= cursor and hi >= cursor always hold, and saturating_sub is ordinary subtraction that avoids the overflow in cursor+n. A hostile huge n gives OutOfMemory in both: the model finds no gap, and the kernel's find_virtual_address checked_sub fails, which map_run turns into OutOfMemory.
> - R11MapFixedSkipsOverlap bites: it is caught through the leaked frame (R6), not by a 'never replaces' property. That is acceptable.
> 
> Findings:
> P2-1 tests/programs/src/bin/map-fixed-attack.rs:92-105: nothing tests the 'page tables' half of the charge check, in the kernel or the model. free+1 pages is refused by the pages check alone. That second check is the only thing that keeps an under-count in tables_needed from reaching the .expect at mem.rs:1285/1293 and panicking the kernel. Plan v2 item: fill with map_anon until free == npages+tables-1, then map_fixed a 2-page range that crosses a 2 MiB boundary in an unused GiB (e.g. 0x1_0000_0000-0x1000 on rv64, which needs an L1 table plus 2 L0 tables, so 5 pages). Expect OutOfMemory with usage unchanged. Free one more page and expect success with usage exactly +5.
> P2-2 :71-76: the untouched legacy reservation isn't tested. The stack is reserved as [sp-128K, sp) (services.rs:482, arch/riscv/process.rs:396), so USER_STACK_TOP - 128*1024 is an untouched reservation. Add refused(c, "untouched stack reservation", USER_STACK_TOP - DEFAULT_STACK_SIZE, PAGE, ...). Today, changing subtree_occupied's !is_empty() to is_occupied passes every test.
> P2-3 :107-120: 'huge len promptly' has no teeth. 1 GiB is 2^18 pages, so a regression to one walk per page takes milliseconds and never trips the 30 s timeout. Use addr 0x1_0000_0000, len USER_AREA_END - 0x1_0000_0000 (about 2^26 pages, free on rv64, since the stack sits below 0x8000_0000), and assert that the time_now delta is under a bound such as 10 ms.
> P2-4: the lent-in and lent-out cases from plan v2 are missing. The kernel refuses them only because S-bit PTEs are non-empty, and the model's check is a different mechanism (LentIn/LentOut in p.space). Add them, or get an explicit orchestrator waiver.
> P3-5 :61: 'straddles USER_AREA_END' uses USER_AREA_END - PAGE/2, which is unaligned, so the alignment check refuses it first. The model test at map_fixed_contracts.rs:85 does the same. A real straddle is addr USER_AREA_END - PAGE with len 2*PAGE.
> P3-6 :143-155: the last page is unmapped before the map_anon check, so the kernel half of P1-1 (map_anon while a page just below USER_AREA_END is mapped) isn't exercised. Keep it mapped across the map_anon call.
> P3-7: 'flags enforced' tests only that an RW page is writable. A write to an R-only page faulting (via attack-checker) is still missing.
> P3-8 libs/sys/src/tests.rs, user_range_at_width: this tests a copy of the check, not the kernel's user_range (a cfg(baremetal) function), so a change to the kernel wouldn't fail it. It's fine as documentation; say so, or share the function.

> PLAN v1, part 1/6: context, and section 1 (kernel-owned timer)
> 
> CONTEXT
> - Scheduling today is cooperative and PID round-robin: kmain's next_pid_to_run does SwitchTo, and threads run until they block or yield.
> - The hart timer is legacy IRQ 0. That covers timer_sbi.rs, irq.rs's timer::owns branches, platform/sbi/mod.rs TIMER_TIMEBASE/TIMER_SET_DEADLINE, and the timer-test program with its timer.toml case (also used in all-together.toml).
> - Redoubt timeouts exist as data. W_DEADLINE in each thread's IPC page is set by message::mark, but message::expire runs only at Redoubt syscalls (redoubt.rs:46) and in a polling idle loop (main.rs:147).
> - Budgets record weight and deadline (budget.rs), and nothing enforces either.
> - The model (model/src/sched.rs; kernel.rs tick/expire) already has a stride queue, logical time, timeouts and budget deadlines. But ties go to the lower budget id, tick re-picks at every event (so a timeout wake preempts), and a sleeper keeps a stale pass across an idle instant.
> 
> 1. TIMER
> - Backend is SBI TIME (sbi_rt::set_timer), not Sstc. It works under both prototyper builds and every SBI platform, including the planned FPGA softcores, and it is the code already in timer_sbi.rs. Sstc needs firmware to set menvcfg.STCE, and nothing tests that. RESOURCES permits Sstc by capability feature; I won't add an untested backend. One ecall per arming at a 10 ms slice is negligible.
> - New kernel/src/time.rs (portable), with timer_sbi.rs reduced to the backend:
>   - now_us() is unchanged.
>   - ticks_at(us) rounds up and saturates (FOREVER -> u64::MAX). The interrupt never fires before the µs deadline, so every interrupt finds something due and nothing livelocks.
>   - arm/disarm.
>   - Cached earliest-deadline hints: mark() lowers the thread hint and budget_create lowers the budget hint; expire recomputes both exactly. A stale hint is only ever early, costing one spurious interrupt, so nothing is missed (I13).
>   - Always armed while running: min(slice_end, earliest timeout, earliest budget deadline). Idle: min(deadlines), or disarm if there are none.
>   - Boot fails closed if the loader gave no Time timebase. Today it is max(1), which silently makes µs wrong.
> - Expiry: time::expire_due runs at every timer interrupt, at every kernel entry (legacy and Redoubt syscalls, external IRQs), and before a Redoubt call returns. This mirrors the model, which expires after every op. The hint makes the usual case one compare.
> - Due order is the model's: earliest deadline first; at an equal instant, timeouts before budget deadlines, then thread order or budget id. It matters. A caller in Reply whose timeout and whose server budget's deadline have both passed gets Timeout with the lend consumed if the timeout goes first, and Dead with the lend returned if the budget goes first. Today's expire takes the first match in walk order, so it is replaced.
> - rdtime: scounteren.TM is already set; K5 keeps and tests it. How user mode learns the frequency is question K5-q-timebase.
> - IRQ-0 removal:
>   - delete timer::IRQ, owns, mask and unmask, and the IRQ-0 dispatch in arch/riscv/irq.rs; SupervisorTimerInterrupt goes to time::on_interrupt only;
>   - platform_call timer ops are deleted and return UnhandledSyscall (K6 removes the plumbing), and the constants go from libs/abi/src/arch/riscv/mem.rs;
>   - delete tests/timer.toml and timer-test.rs, and drop timer-test with its irq=[0] grant from all-together.toml;
>   - fix the irq.rs doc comment;
>   - disable_all_irqs stops masking the timer;
>   - remove the polling idle branch, so idle is wfi with the timer armed.
>   - Loader and device.rs refusal of source 0 is unchanged (PLIC 0 doesn't exist).

Event: `e005b826285c5a246103b479df209f91` · 2026-09-24T17:51:08Z

> PLAN v1, part 2/6: section 2 (one stride queue over every runnable budget)
> 
> - State lives in the budget frame, as words after the current 16+MAX_LABELS: pass (u128, two words), tie (i64), queued (bool), and a round-robin cursor (pid, tid). Per-hart state is one KernelCell<Hart> in new kernel/src/sched.rs: running budget, slice start/end, switched_in. It is written so SMP can make it per hart.
> - Pure logic goes in a new crate libs/stride (redoubt-stride: no_std, zero deps, zero unsafe): step and wake arithmetic, ordering key, tie counters. It is host-tested and used by the kernel. The model keeps its own implementation; a dev-only differential test in libs/stride replays random sequences through both and requires identical picks and passes. The model gains no kernel dependency.
> - Arithmetic: step = min(runtime, 2^40) * STRIDE / weight, all in u64 (product < 2^60); pass: u128 += step.
>   - u128 is only used for add and compare, which are cheap on rv32 with no u128 mul/div. Starting at 0 at creation, it can't overflow in any lifetime.
>   - u128 is the model's type too, so there's no wrap logic.
>   - Everything is checked or saturating, so the overflow checks in checked builds can't panic (I14). Weight is never 0 (process_created already refuses weight-0 budgets).
> - Charging happens at EVERY deschedule. The one choke point is SystemServices::activate_process_thread, whenever the running (pid, tid) changes. That covers kmain dispatch, blocking (settle), yield, slice preemption, exit, and the legacy direct switches (borrowed-quantum send_message, IRQ callbacks). Each charge goes to the budget of the process that actually ran. PID 1 (kmain/idle) is charged to nobody. Runtime is counted in time ticks with a minimum of 1 per deschedule, so sub-µs bursts can't go free (K5-q-units).
> - Pick: kmain replaces next_pid_to_run with sched::pick.
>   - It walks the <=64 processes, collects budgets with a runnable thread, and takes the lowest (pass, tie, budget id).
>   - Inside that budget it takes the next runnable (pid, tid) after the budget's cursor: round-robin over all threads of all its processes (R12).
>   - Then SwitchTo, slice_end = now + SLICE, arm.
> - Wake: pass = max(own, current minimum).
>   - A wake is a budget going from 0 runnable threads to at least 1.
>   - Wakes are reconciled once per kernel entry, just before leaving the kernel, by comparing the runnable set with each budget's queued flag. That avoids hooking the dozen legacy ProcessState writers in services.rs; the model mirrors it once per op.
>   - Current minimum = the lowest pass of queued budgets, counting the running budget at its last-charged pass, floored by a monotone virtual-time floor that survives an empty queue (K5-q-minimum).
>   - Without the floor, a sleeper that wakes while nothing else is runnable keeps its old low pass, then starves everyone until it catches up. The model has this hole; its fairness generator always keeps a spinner running, so it never sees it.
> - Ties are deterministic and wake-first. tie is an i64 from two global counters:
>   - a wake takes front -= 1, so it ranks ahead of every queued equal;
>   - a requeue after deschedule (slice end, or a deadline re-pick with threads still runnable) takes back += 1, FIFO behind equals;
>   - wakes reconciled in the same entry go in ascending budget id (K5-q-ties).
>   Ties are the common case: every wake whose own pass is <= the minimum lands exactly on the minimum.
> - Preemption only at slice end or a deadline:
>   - A timer interrupt at slice_end charges the running budget, requeues it, and switches to kmain to re-pick. This is a forced yield through the existing activate_process_thread path with can_resume = true.
>   - A BUDGET deadline destroys the budget (section 4) and then re-picks.
>   - Timeout expiry and IRQ wakes only make threads runnable; the running thread keeps its slice (K5-q-preempt).
>   - A thread that blocks ends its own slice. Legacy direct switches continue the slice.

Event: `b709819964e5ed28c5196143f055699b` · 2026-09-24T17:51:19Z

> PLAN v1, part 3/6: sections 3 (timeouts) and 4 (budget deadlines)
> 
> 3. TIMEOUTS on call/send/receive
> - Representation is unchanged: W_DEADLINE in the thread IPC page = now + timeout, saturating; FOREVER never expires. mark() also lowers the time hint. settle() keeps its immediate Timeout for a deadline that has already passed (a poll). No new object and no allocation.
> - Armed in mark() via the hint, then time::rearm on the way out of the kernel.
> - Cancellation is implicit. wake, fail_wait, thread_ending and finish_served all set W_WAIT = None, and expiry ignores a deadline whose wait is None. A stale hint costs one spurious interrupt.
> - Races: one hart, SIE clear in the kernel, one lock, so kernel entry order decides everything. expire_due runs first at every entry, so a passed deadline beats any operation that enters later.
>   - Reply vs timeout: the reply's entry expires the caller first. Caller: Timeout, lend consumed, reply absent. Server's reply: discarded, mask 0 (IPC completion row 2). A reply before the deadline wins normally, and W_WAIT=None cancels the timeout.
>   - Queued call/send timeout: Timeout, lend/transfer returned (row 1). This is already fail_wait/unwind/give_buffer_back.
>   - Abandon: a Reply-waiter timing out abandons the call (R3): abandon(), then the server's one notice (I15), then pump. Already in fail_wait.
>   - Exit: a caller that dies first goes through thread_ending, so no timeout fires later. A server that dies first gives its caller Dead with the lend returned (row 3). Same-instant timeout and budget deadline use the fixed due order from section 1.
>   - Receive on an IRQ times out as today; R5 keeps the source masked until the next receive.
> - I13: every blocked thread with a finite deadline has its call completed (result committed, made runnable) by the first kernel entry at or after its deadline, and the timer guarantees there is such an entry. When it then runs is R12's business (K5-q-preempt).
> 
> 4. BUDGET DEADLINES
> - Refactor redoubt::budget_destroy into budget::destroy(ss, top, caller: Option<PID>). The syscall and the deadline path share it, so both use exactly today's R10 order:
>   (1) destroy_begin marks the subtree dying.
>   (2) Every process in it is killed, other processes first and the caller last (the deadline path has no caller).
>       - Notice: `killed` unless the creator is dying or the endpoint is dead; R1 applies; blame is always 0.
>       - Each thread goes through thread_ending (R4b). A pending call unwinds. A call held as server fails its caller with Dead and the lend returned. An abandoned lend is freed.
>   (3) process::budgets_dying frees process objects charged to the subtree, with no notice.
>   (4) message::budgets_dying:
>       - owned endpoints and devices are destroyed, and their waiters get Dead;
>       - queued messages sent through stamped handles fail with Dead;
>       - taken ones fail with Dead and are abandoned (R3), and the lend stays mapped in the server, charged to it, until its reply.
>   (5) destroy_marked sweeps handles everywhere, including unreceived messages, and returns limits to the parent (I10 once notices are received).
> - The deadline entry point is destroy_frame(top), which takes a frame, not a handle. Today pid is used only for handle lookup and the caller-last order.
> - expire_due destroys due budgets earliest (deadline, id) first, and skips descendants already destroyed with an ancestor.
> - A deadline already passed at budget_create is destroyed at that syscall's exit expiry; the returned handle is revoked at its next use. This matches the model, which expires after the op.
> - If the running process died, the trap returns to kmain (the Outcome::Resume / caller_doomed logic). The re-pick is as in section 2. root, system and users are FOREVER.

> PLAN v1, part 4/6: sections 5 (SMP and icache) and 6 (model)
> 
> 5. SMP
> - K5 stays single-hart for scheduling: one global queue under the existing big lock (KernelCell, which is a spinlock under `smp'), per RESOURCES' SMP stance.
> - Per-hart state is isolated in sched::Hart, and the SBI timer is per hart, so the post-M1 SMP work can split them.
> - The `smp' feature must build and smp-spike must pass on both widths. The spike runs before the scheduler and never arms the secondary's timer.
> - K5 claims nothing about multi-hart scheduling or IPC1 concurrent completion.
> - Icache (R2-followups item 5): the kernel has no fence.i.
>   - On one hart, a parent writes a child's code (process_map, or the stub via map_fixed), and nothing orders those stores before the child's first fetch.
>   - A physically tagged icache could also hold a previous owner's code for a recycled frame. That is a correctness hazard, not a privilege one: it runs in the new owner's context.
>   - Proposal: K5 owns only the single-hart piece. One fence.i right before a started process's first thread first runs (process_start), as its own small commit, adding 1 unsafe asm in arch/riscv. The multi-hart piece (fence on migration, or SBI remote fence.i) stays with the SMP work.
>   - QEMU can't observe it, so the evidence is code review. Question K5-q-icache.
> 
> 6. MODEL
> Files: model/src/sched.rs, kernel.rs (tick, expire, wake reconciliation), mutation.rs, check.rs, invariants.rs, tests/mutations.rs, README/VALIDATION counts.
> - Stride queue:
>   - add a tie key with front/back counters;
>   - reconcile wakes once per op, in ascending budget id;
>   - the minimum includes the running budget and the monotone floor (per the K5-q-minimum answer);
>   - a charge requeues at the back.
> - Running slice: the scheduler gains current: Option<(budget, tid, slice_start)>.
>   - tick runs `current' until the earliest of slice end, the op's end, or a BUDGET deadline.
>   - Timeouts and IRQs wake without a re-pick.
>   - A thread that blocks ends `current'. timer() stays slice end or next deadline.
> - expire already orders earliest first, timeouts ahead of budgets. Add a focused test that pins the Reply-timeout vs server-deadline outcome.
> - New properties:
>   (a) Ties: at a pick among equal passes, the budget woken latest wins.
>   (b) Preemption points: `current' changes only at slice end, block, exit or a budget deadline.
>   (c) Idle-gap banking: every budget sleeps at once, then a stale-pass sleeper wakes first; its share over the following interval stays within the bound.
>   (d) Sub-slice gaming: SLICE-eps run, 1 µs sleep, repeat; its share stays <= its weight plus the bound.
>   (e) The I13 check stays, plus a check that completion lands at the deadline tick.
> - New mutations, each with its catching property:
>   - R12TieQueuedFirst: (a) plus a focused example;
>   - R12PreemptOnWake: (b);
>   - R12NoFloorWhenIdle: (c);
>   - R12ShortRunsFree (runs under a slice charge 0): (d);
>   - R12RequeueAhead: (a);
>   - TimeoutIgnoredWhileOthersRun (expiry only when idle): I13;
>   - ExpireBudgetsFirst (equal-instant order): the focused outcome test.
>   - Existing R12PriorityById, R12IgnoreWeight, R12WakeBanksCredit and BudgetDeadlineIgnored must still be caught.
> - Evidence: the default suites, --test mutations (all detected), and one `million' run at the end, with counts in VALIDATION.md.
> - Differential: libs/stride dev tests replay random wake/block/charge/pick/deadline sequences through the stride crate (as the kernel wires it) and through redoubt_model::sched::Scheduler, and require identical picks and passes.

> PLAN v1, part 5/6: section 7 (tests)
> 
> Every boot case is kind=boot, arch rv64+rv32, a checked build.
> - Verdicts come from a trusted launcher/checker: the bundle's first program, which holds root/system/users and every device object.
> - Children are spawned with tests/programs/src/spawn.rs (a copy of the caller).
> - Spinners run the same counted loop, so a count ratio is a CPU-share ratio.
> - Tolerances are fixed in each case and justified from the model bound.
> 
> - sched-share (spinning budget bounded by weight): budgets 100/100/300 in `users', each spinning for T. Count ratios must be within tolerance of the weight ratios, and a victim's share must be >= w/W - tol.
> - sched-sleep-gaming (sleep/wake gaming): the gamer runs just under a slice, then sleeps 1 µs, repeating. Variants: long sleep then burst, and an idle-gap wake. Gamer share <= its weight share + tol; the equal-weight victim >= its share - tol.
> - sched-server-busy (system server busy on one user): a system-class server (weight 100 from `system') spins per request. User A floods it; users B and C spin. B and C must keep their shares - tol; A's flood buys only the server's weight.
> - sched-large-weight: a server at 1000 against N=8 users at 100, all spinning. Server share >= 1000/1800 - tol. The check is repeated inside the latency bench.
> - timeouts (I13, real timer; this closes IPC1's real-timers gate on the K5 side):
>   - sleep with the system otherwise IDLE (no syscalls anywhere, which proves the timer, not polling), and again with a spinner running;
>   - queued call (lend returned) and send time out;
>   - a taken call times out: lend consumed, the server gets one notice, and its reply is discarded;
>   - receive on an endpoint and on an IRQ;
>   - FOREVER, and near-u64::MAX saturation;
>   - 200 iterations of a reply racing the deadline at random offsets; each outcome must be one of the two legal rows;
>   - lateness reported;
>   - rdtime from U-mode: monotonic, rv32 hi/lo consistent, linear against time_now.
> - budget-deadline:
>   - Setup: a lease budget with a deadline, holding spinning children; a lend taken by a server outside it; a queued send; handles stamped with it held elsewhere; a child budget with a later deadline.
>   - Checks: killed notices with blame 0; the abandoned notice exactly once; Dead to the sender; handles 0 or BadHandle; parent usage restored (I10); a deadline already past at creation destroys the budget at once; FOREVER never fires; deadline-to-notice lateness reported.
>   - The running spinner covers preemption at a deadline.
> - sched-ties:
>   - New kernel feature sched-trace: a bounded in-kernel ring of wake/pick records {budget, weight, pass, tie, reason}, printed at system_reset.
>   - Sleepers at equal weight wake into a queue of spinners. The kernel prints a summary, and the case expects every equal-pass pick to choose the latest waker.
>   - The exact order is proven by the libs/stride host tests on the kernel's own code, by the differential and by the model mutations.
> - stride-host-tests (kind=host-tests, redoubt-stride). model-host-tests is unchanged.
> - The IRQ-0 `timer' case is deleted.
> - Every existing boot case is re-run on both widths, since preemption changes timing everywhere. The consoled flood case gets 1 cargo test plus the binary x20, no loops.
> 
> sched-latency, the named-workload bench:
> - Workload: N in {1,4,16} user budgets at weight 100 (INIT's user weight), each spinning; a driver at 1000 and a steward at 1000 (INIT), carved the way INIT carves them.
> - Driver: owns the QEMU virt goldfish RTC (its MMIO and IRQ device objects). K times: program the alarm at a random future RTC time T, receive on the IRQ handle, then read RTC time. Latency = t - T, on the RTC's own clock.
> - Steward stand-in: K times: create a lease under `users' and spawn a spinner in it; sleep until a random T (receive(none, timeout)); budget_destroy(lease); latency = time_now after destroy - T. The kernel-deadline lease path (deadline to killed notice) is also reported.
> - Recorded: weights, runnable-budget count and each budget's prior pass at every measured wake (from the sched-trace ring), and p50/p99/max for each N. The large-weight share check runs under the same load.
> - Target proposal:
>   - I post the table in this thread and propose a target, for example p99 <= X ms and max <= Y ms for N <= 16 on QEMU TCG, read off the data with margin.
>   - I expect about one slice (<= 10 ms plus overhead), since with 10x the weight the driver's own pass rarely exceeds the minimum.
>   - After reviewer acceptance, a final commit pins the target as the case's pass condition.
> - TCG timing follows host load, so I'd like a per-case QEMU `-icount shift=auto' option in the testbench.
> - The steward and drivers are stand-ins, since neither boots natively before R3/S2. Both points are asked in K5-q-bench.

> PLAN v1.1: K5-q-preempt answered (recommendations a and b). Changes to the plan:
> - The only preemption points are slice end and a BUDGET deadline. A timeout expiry or IRQ is a wake (pass = max(own, min), wake-first tie), and the running thread keeps its slice.
> - A budget deadline re-picks whichever budget's deadline fired: the running budget's partial slice is charged and it is requeued at the back (FIFO behind equals).
>   - New sub-case in budget-deadline: the deadline of a budget that is NOT running fires while a spinner runs. The sched-trace record must show the spinner charged a partial slice and a re-pick, and the destroyed budget's lateness is reported.

The always-armed timer bounds that entry by timer latency. When the thread then runs is R12's business. > - New mutation R12TimeoutWakePreempts: a timeout wake re-picks. It is caught by the slice-ownership property (b), where `current` changes only at slice end, block, exit or a budget deadline, plus a focused example: a spinner in mid-slice when a sleeper's timeout expires at an equal pass. > PLAN v1.2: K5-q-minimum answered (approved as defined). Changes to the plan:
> - Current minimum = the lowest pass among runnable budgets, including the running one at its last-charged pass. The floor is a monotone value that rises to that minimum whenever it changes and holds when the queue empties. Wake pass = max(own, floor).
> - Overflow (section 2): the floor has the same type as pass, u128, on rv32 and rv64.
>   - It is only compared and raised by max, never wrapped.
>   - It starts at 0 and never exceeds the largest pass. A pass can't overflow: each step is < 2^60 (runtime capped at 2^40 ticks x 2^20 / weight >= 1), and even 2^64 such steps stay far below 2^128.
>   - So no wrap-safe comparison is needed on either width. Passes and the floor use plain u128 ordering, which is also the model's type. All arithmetic is checked or saturating (I14).
> - New budgets: KERNEL-SPEC's budget table and R12 say nothing about an initial pass, and budget_create takes no scheduling argument. A budget starts at pass 0, and its first runnable thread is a wake, so it enters at max(0, floor) = floor. A new thread in an already-queued budget doesn't move the budget. Nothing in the spec contradicts this.
> - Docs commit: a one-line R12 clarification next to the I13 one.
> - Model: the same rule, plus mutation R12NoFloorWhenIdle, caught by the idle-gap property (c).
> - New boot case sched-idle-gap (rv64 and rv32, checked build, verdict from the launcher):
>   - A (weight 100) sleeps while B (weight 100) runs alone for about 2 s, so A's own pass stays far below B's.
>   - B blocks for a short gap (receive(none, timeout), about 5 ms). A's timeout is placed inside that gap, using absolute times the launcher computes from time_now, so A wakes while nothing else is runnable.
>   - Both then spin for a window W. Pass condition: B's work >= 1/2 - tol of the total. Without the floor, A would monopolise the CPU for about 2 s.
>   - Companion sub-case: a budget created and started during the gap must also enter at the floor, so its share over W is <= 1/2 + tol.
> - sched-idle-gap joins commit 5. The boot case count is now 10.

Event: `f64c487884a182dc387de6bcc5fd1fd1` · 2026-09-24T17:54:19Z

> PLAN v1.3: K5-q-ties answered (approved, with precisions). Changes to the plan:
> - RANK RULE among runnable budgets with an equal pass:
>   (1) every waker ranks ahead of every requeued budget;
>   (2) a wake in a later kernel entry (or model op) ranks ahead of one in an earlier entry (LIFO across entries);
>   (3) among wakes in the same entry, the lower budget id ranks ahead;
>   (4) requeues rank FIFO.
> - Implementation: the key is (pass, tie, id). Same-entry wakes are processed in DESCENDING budget id, each taking front -= 1, so the lowest id gets the frontmost key. A requeue takes back += 1.
> - Budget ids come from the kernel's next_object_id counter (budget.rs). They are never reused (I12), and no call takes an id, so no process can pick an id to win simultaneous ties. The only lever is creating a budget earlier to get an older, lower id. That affects only same-entry ties at an equal pass, and each run's charge advances the winner's pass, so the others still get their turn.
> - A wake is a budget going from zero runnable threads to at least one. Another thread of an already-queued budget becoming runnable doesn't move it.
> - Tie counters: front and back are i64s kept in u64 kernel words, the same on rv32 and rv64 (64-bit software arithmetic on rv32).
>   - Each moves by one per wake or requeue, so reaching 2^63 takes 2^63 scheduler events, centuries at one per ns.
>   - The arithmetic is saturating anyway, so no panic (I14). Saturation would only make those ties fall back to id order.
>   - Both reset to 0 whenever the queue is empty (no key is live then), which also keeps them small. The model does the same.
> - Mutations R12TieQueuedFirst and R12RequeueAhead are kept. The model differential and host tests pin the exact rank, including same-entry id order.
> - Boot case sched-ties (sched-trace kernel feature, rv64 and rv32). It exercises:
>   (i) a sleeper waking at the floor ties with the queued spinner, and the sleeper runs first;
>   (ii) two sleepers with timeouts at the same instant wake in one kernel entry at an equal pass: lower id first, then higher, both ahead of the spinner;
>   (iii) a slice-end requeue goes behind equals.
>   The kernel prints a summary of every equal-pass pick with its rank reason; the case expects all three patterns and forbids any violation line.
> - One KERNEL-SPEC docs commit carries all three clarifications: I13, current minimum/floor, and ties/rank.

> PLAN v1.4: K5-q-units answered (approved, plus an exact remainder). Changes to the plan:
> - Charging is in timebase ticks, with a minimum of 1 per deschedule and runtime capped at 2^40 ticks. Timeouts and deadlines stay in µs per the ABI.
> - EXACT REMAINDER (overflow section): each budget frame gains a word rem.
>   - At each charge: t = rem + ticks x STRIDE; step = t / weight; rem = t % weight; pass (u128) += step.
>   - Bounds: ticks x STRIDE <= 2^40 x 2^20 = 2^60, and rem < weight <= 2^32 - 1, so t < 2^61 fits u64 on rv32 and rv64. No saturation is needed on this path; it is checked arithmetic that can't fail.
>   - Charging is then exact over any sequence and never free for any weight. There is no step >= 1 floor, which would overcharge large weights.
>   - rem is set to 0 only at budget creation. A wake doesn't clear it: raising the pass to the floor doesn't erase fractional debt.
>   - Today's weights are carved from ROOT_WEIGHT = 1000 (budget.rs), so none can currently exceed 2^20. But the ABI field is a u32, and without the carry even small weights lose up to one unit per deschedule. So the remainder is unconditional.
> - Model: stays in µs, since the differential against libs/stride runs in one unit, and carries the same rem.
>   - Its batched charge_slices stays exact: carrying the remainder across n charges equals one charge of the total, so batching is still identical to slice-by-slice.
>   - New mutation R12DropRemainder (step = floor, remainder discarded), caught by an extension of the gaming property (d): a weight-2^24 budget running 1 µs bursts against an equal-weight spinner must stay within its share. Under the mutation its pass never advances.
>   - R12ShortRunsFree stays for sub-slice runs charged 0. The mutation count is now 9.
> - The KERNEL-SPEC clarification commit's R12 line gains: runtime is charged in ticks with an exact per-budget remainder.
> - The libs/stride host tests add exhaustive small-weight checks and random large-weight checks: the sum of steps over any split of a runtime equals the step of the total, given the carried remainder.

Event: `791d69acfea2339b8d83c5143845b806` · 2026-09-24T17:56:08Z

> PLAN v1.6: K5-q-icache answered (K5 owns the single-hart piece). I checked every path. Commit 7 now fences at X installation, not only at process_start.
> 
> Paths to executable bytes:
> - Lends and transfers are mapped R|W only (arch/riscv/mem.rs map_into), so they are never X in the receiver. A transferred page becomes X only through the receiver's own set_flags. A borrowed page can't be set_flags'd (not the caller's own mapping).
> - map_device and dma_alloc map R|W.
> - process_map is refused once the child has started (process.rs:366, NotPermitted). The kernel never installs X into a running process except at that process's own request: map_anon/map_fixed with X, or set_flags adding X.
> - W^X (R11): a page's contents can change only while it isn't X. So every write-then-fetch path, whoever wrote the bytes, passes through a kernel call that installs X: process_map, map_anon, map_fixed or set_flags. The writer can be the parent, the owner, the kernel's zeroing, or DMA into a dma_alloc page.
> 
> Decision: the kernel fences, rather than making it the process's job.
> - arch::riscv::mem::sync_icache() is one fence.i, the only new unsafe asm.
> - It runs after any successful call that installs or adds X (process_map, map_anon, map_fixed, set_flags), before the return to user mode, and once at boot before the first user dispatch, which covers loader-written images.
> - On one hart this orders every earlier store before any fetch through the new mapping, so no process needs its own fence.i for memory it got through syscalls. U-mode fence.i stays legal and harmless (the stub keeps its own).
> 
> Recycled frames: a stale, physically tagged line can only be fetched through an X mapping, and every X installation is followed by the kernel's fence.i on this hart. That instruction synchronises the hart's instruction stream with all earlier stores, including the kernel's zeroing of the recycled frame.
> - Under a "process's responsibility" rule, a hostile new owner could map RX, skip the fence, and execute a victim's stale code, which is a cross-process confidentiality leak. That's why the fence belongs in the kernel.
> 
> Multi-hart (not K5): X installation on one hart doesn't fence the others, and migration needs a fence on the destination hart (or SBI remote fence.i). It stays with post-M1 SMP (PLAN, SMP) and is noted in QA R2-followups item 5.
> 
> Commit 7 is its own small commit, with the unsafe ratchet updated honestly (+1). The argument above goes in the commit message for the red team. The evidence is code review only; QEMU can't observe it.

> PLAN v2: every K5-plan-review finding, with its disposition. This is on top of v1.1 plus the orchestrator's P1-2 rule. Still PLAN ONLY. The full consistent text, which supersedes v1 where they differ, is at /home/mick/.claude/plans/wash-inbox-1-message-iterative-comet.md.
> 
> P1-1 FREE CPU ON EXIT PATHS: ACCEPTED; accounting moves to the trap boundary.
> - There are exactly two sret sites, _redoubt_resume_context (via arch::syscall::resume) and _redoubt_syscall_return_result (via irq.rs return_registers), and one trap entry, trap_handler.
> - EXIT HOOK (resume/return_registers, when returning to U): if the target's budget differs from Hart.running, deschedule the old budget (fold, requeue with back += 1) and set running. Then record user_since and user_budget as a (frame, id) BudgetRef, and rearm.
> - ENTRY HOOK (first thing in trap_handler when SPP=User, before anything reads the process): pending += now - user_since, for user_budget.
> - No U-mode instruction runs outside a return/entry pair, so thread_exit (destroy_thread -> switch_to_thread), process_exit, faults, kills (terminate_process -> switch_to_thread) and callback switches can't skip it.
> - Passes still change only at a FOLD: a budget change at exit, a kmain pick, a slice-end or deadline preemption, or a destroy. So R12's "at every deschedule" holds literally, and the exact remainder makes the split charges equal the total.
> - New boot case sched-exit-churn: thread churn plus process exit and fault churn; victim share >= 1/2 - tol, asserted.
> - New model mutation R12ExitRunsFree (exit/fault/kill of `current' drops its partial run), caught by the new exit-churn fairness property (f).
> 
> P1-2 BUDGET CHURN: ORCHESTRATOR RULE R6, a pass inherited through the tree, to be confirmed by the owner.
> - Create: child pass = max(floor, PARENT budget pass), rem = 0.
> - Destroy (syscall, deadline or revocation): bottom-up in R10 order, before destroy_marked, fold the dying budget's pending time (including a running one), then parent.pass = max(parent, child).
> - Proof it closes the loop: a pass is a virtual-time position, the point up to which a budget has been served.
>   - Loop create C, run, destroy: C starts at >= P.pass. When destroyed it leaves P.pass >= C's final pass = start + (run x STRIDE)/w_C. The next child starts there.
>   - So the sequence of children is charged exactly like one continuous budget of weight w_C whose pass carries over, and gains nothing over running in the parent.
>   - Concurrent siblings each run fairly at their own weights. The parent takes max(c_i), so a successor starts no earlier than any sibling's service point.
>   - max is right and a sum would double-count: the siblings consumed in parallel while the floor advanced.
>   - Carving is unaffected: weight returns to the parent at destroy (R7), and pass is a position, not an amount, so nothing is counted twice.
>   - Loss: rem < w_C at destroy, i.e. under 1 pass unit per destroyed budget, and every creation is itself a charged syscall.
> - Parking variant (a fresh intermediate M per cycle): each M holds >= 1 carved weight until it is destroyed, and destroying it pushes its debt up. So parked free entries are bounded by the attacker budget's weight limit, and any destroy repays them.
> - Cross-subtree residual: a child's pass is <= floor + one step (a runnable budget only runs at the minimum), so debt parked on a shared parent (users/system) delays later siblings by at most one slice at the child's weight. Only init and the steward create there, at manifest weights >= 100. This is stated.
> - New boot case sched-budget-churn: weight-1 child create/run-one-slice/destroy loop, plus the parking variant. Asserted: victim >= 1/2 - tol, attacker subtree <= 1/2 + tol.
> - New model mutations R12DestroyDropsDebt and R12CreateAtFloorOnly, both caught by the churn property (g), which includes parking.
> - The R12/R7 clarification goes in the docs commit.
> 
> P1-3 EXPIRY KILLS STATE THE TRAP CAPTURED: ACCEPTED; per-entry protocol, with no expect() on a killable pid.
> - kmain (PID 1) SwitchTo entry: NO expiry. kmain runs expire_due -> reconcile -> fold -> pick -> SwitchTo with no entry in between. A failed SwitchTo re-picks and no longer panics.
> - Redoubt and legacy ecalls from U: entry hook -> expire_due -> re-read current; if the caller's (pid, tid) is gone, skip the call and resume current; otherwise dispatch with the re-read pid.
> - External IRQ from U: re-read after expiry, BEFORE PREVIOUS_PAIR is recorded.
> - Timer from U: after expiry, if current died -> kmain; the slice check otherwise.
> - Timer or IRQ from S (idle): expiry, then resume PID 1.
> - EXIT_THREAD, RETURN_FROM_ISR, RETURN_FROM_EXCEPTION_HANDLER and faults: after expiry, if the thread died, skip thread_exit/faulted/fault handling and resume current.
> - expire_due runs once per entry. A past-deadline budget_create is destroyed at the next entry.
> 
> P2-1 LEGACY CALLBACKS: ACCEPTED as a guard plus a stated residual.
> - While PREVIOUS_PAIR is set, timeouts still expire (they only wake), but budget-deadline destruction and slice-end preemption are deferred to just after finish_isr's resume, through the normal path.
> - finish_isr with a dead previous pair resumes current instead of expect().
> - The preempt path activates PID 1 directly with SWITCHTO_CALLER reset: no do_yield, no expect.
> - Residual until K6: a callback that never returns keeps the CPU. Only manifest-granted IRQs can be claimed (grants::may_claim_irq; interrupt_claim refuses device-object IRQs), and after K5 the only claimants are the irq-attack/grant-attack refusal tests. The v1 claim that "a callback can't hold off slice ends" is withdrawn.
> 
> P2-2 THE DEADLINE PATH ISN'T CALLER-LESS: ACCEPTED.
> - If the interrupted current process is in the doomed subtree, it is the caller, killed last via process::killed; the path returns to kmain. kill_process never targets current.
> - Hart.running is a (frame, id) BudgetRef with a liveness check. Pending time is folded and propagated (R6), and dying budgets are purged from the queued set and Hart.running, all before destroy_marked frees frames. No scheduling word is written into a freed or reused frame.
> 
> P2-3 KERNEL WORK BILLED TO THE VICTIM: ACCEPTED, with a billing rule.
> - U-mode time goes to the budget that ran it.
> - Syscall time (entry to exit) goes to the caller's budget, folded during destroy if the call kills that budget.
> - Expiry work, wherever it runs and including the one shared walk, goes to the budget of the FIRST due item in due order: a timeout's thread budget, or a deadline's dying budget.

> - Bound: at most O(1) uncharged kernel work per charged syscall, and nothing is billed to a victim.

>   - free weights sum to at most root's, so a subtree's long-run share is at most its free-weight share;
>   - waits are inherited unscaled and max never lowers an ancestor, so create/destroy without a run gains nothing;
>   - residual per destroy: a remainder under 1 unit, plus the w_child/w_parent conversion of the inherited entry wait, which is at most one ancestor step because a child runs only at the minimum;

A walk runs only when the hint is due, and a hint is early only after a cancel or destroy, each of which follows a charged syscall. ## K5 · K5-q-preempt — R12/I13: which timer events preempt; what 'returns by its timeout' means

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 3

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

### K5 implementer · Question

Event: `f81ffc62e3a50d0ff0e7fc260f1acaf9` · 2026-09-24T17:52:34Z

> R12 says preemption happens "at slice end or at a deadline, never on wake alone". RESOURCES' timer has "one deadline queue (slice ends, timeouts, lease deadlines)". So when a thread's timeout expires while another thread is running, is that a preemption point, or only a wake?
> 
> The model re-picks at every timer event today, so a timeout wake preempts. With a spinner running, the choice also decides what I13's "every blocking call returns by its timeout" guarantees.
> 
> Recommendation:
> (a) Only slice end and BUDGET deadlines are preemption points. A budget deadline destroys that budget, then re-picks, charging the running budget's partial slice and requeueing it. A timeout expiry or IRQ only wakes; the running thread keeps its slice.
> (b) I13 means the kernel completes the call (Timeout result committed, thread made runnable) at the first kernel entry at or after the deadline, which the always-armed timer guarantees. When the thread then runs is R12's business.
> 
> The alternative, treating timeouts as preemption points, makes every timer wake preempt, which contradicts "never on wake alone" for sleeping drivers.
> 
> Needed before plan approval: it changes the model's tick and commit 5.
> 
> Ask: go with the recommendation, or specify otherwise.

### Orchestrator · Answer

Event: `dc3a4d97b072ead757a8a43d834e117c` · 2026-09-24T17:52:58Z

> Go with your recommendation (a) and (b). The spec already settles it.
> - "Deadline" in R12 is the budget `deadline` attribute (KERNEL-SPEC budget table: "when it passes, the kernel destroys the budget"). A call's expiry is a "timeout" everywhere (FOREVER row, System calls rows, I13). RESOURCES' deadline queue just shares one hardware timer across slice ends, timeouts and lease deadlines; sharing a timer doesn't make every entry a preemption point.
> - So the preemption points are slice end and budget deadline only. A timeout expiry or an IRQ is a wake (pass = max(own, min), wake-first tie), and the running thread keeps its slice. That's the "never on wake alone" line, and it matches answer 166's "prompt but not bounded".
> - A budget deadline may re-pick: charge the running budget's partial slice and requeue it, as you propose. That holds whichever budget's deadline fired, since the spec allows preemption at any deadline. Say which in the plan and test it.
> - I13: the kernel commits the Timeout result and makes the thread runnable at the first kernel entry at or after the timeout. The always-armed timer bounds that entry by timer latency. When the thread then runs is R12's business. Put this reading in the plan explicitly, and add a one-line clarification to KERNEL-SPEC I13 in the K5 docs commit so the model, kernel and tests share it. The owner sees it at plan approval.
> - The model: change its tick so that a timeout wake no longer re-picks. Add a mutation that makes timeout wakes preempt, and show a test catches it (wake-first plus slice ownership).

### Orchestrator · Resolved

Event: `754fba112caa80ebf24052efa0c8fc31` · 2026-09-24T17:53:06Z

> Evidence: Answered from the spec text. KERNEL-SPEC budget table: `deadline` is the budget attribute whose passing destroys the budget. R12 'preemption at slice end or at a deadline, never on wake alone' therefore means budget deadlines; timeouts and IRQs only wake. I13 reading: the Timeout result is committed and the thread made runnable at the first kernel entry at or after the timeout (always-armed timer); running it is R12's business. The K5 plan states this and adds a one-line I13 clarification; the owner confirms at plan approval.

## K5 · K5-q-minimum — R12: 'current minimum' when the queue is empty, and whether the running budget counts

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 3

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

### K5 implementer · Question

Event: `83e606bfbf220fe7a0f8493eb913f88f` · 2026-09-24T17:52:34Z

> R12 says "on wake, pass = max(own pass, current minimum)". Two cases are unspecified.
> 
> (1) No other budget is runnable at the wake instant, i.e. the system is idle. The model then keeps the waker's own pass. Attack: A sleeps with a low pass while B runs alone, and B's pass climbs. B blocks briefly, the system idles, and A wakes (timed with rdtime). A keeps its stale low pass, so when B wakes at max(B, A) A runs until it catches up. A has banked credit while asleep, which RESOURCES says a waking budget cannot do. The model's fairness generator always keeps a spinner runnable, so it never sees this.
> 
> (2) Does the minimum include the running budget (at its pass as last charged)?
> 
> Recommendation: current minimum = the lowest pass among runnable budgets, including the running one, floored by a monotone virtual-time value. The floor is raised to that minimum whenever it changes, and kept when the queue empties, so wake pass = max(own, floor). That is the standard stride global pass. It changes no weights or shares, only closes the idle-gap bank. The model gets the same rule and a mutation, R12NoFloorWhenIdle, caught by a new idle-gap property.
> 
> Ask: approve the definition, or state another.

## K5 · K5-q-ties — R12 ties: order among several equal-pass wakers; what counts as a wake

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 3

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

### K5 implementer · Question

Event: `958d342eed0c71e9b38bea769ee0f114` · 2026-09-24T17:52:34Z

> R12: "a waking budget is ranked ahead of already-queued budgets with an equal pass". Three orders are open:
> (1) Two budgets wake at different times, both at the same pass. Literally the later one is ahead, since the earlier one was already queued when it woke, which makes wakers LIFO.
> (2) Several budgets become runnable in the same kernel entry. One IRQ plus timeouts expiring together is an example.
> (3) Where does a budget descheduled at slice end with threads still runnable go among equals? It isn't waking.
> 
> Recommendation:
> - (1) Literal: a later wake ranks ahead of earlier queued equals (tie key: wakes take a decreasing counter).
> - (2) Wakes are reconciled once per kernel entry (once per model op), in ascending budget id.
> - (3) A requeue goes FIFO behind equals (tie key: an increasing counter), so a descheduled budget can't win its own tie.
> - A "wake" is a budget going from zero runnable threads to at least one. Another thread of an already-queued budget becoming runnable doesn't move it.
> 
> All of this is deterministic and mirrored in the model, with mutations R12TieQueuedFirst and R12RequeueAhead.
> 
> Ask: approve, or give the order.

## K5 · K5-q-units — R12 charging unit: timebase ticks rather than whole microseconds

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 3

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

### K5 implementer · Question

Event: `12b5c1028061ce65260f73cabcf33e17` · 2026-09-24T17:52:34Z

> R12: "pass += runtime x STRIDE / weight". The spec's time unit is µs. If the kernel measures runtime in whole µs, a thread that runs under 1 µs per burst and blocks is charged 0. That's a sub-µs gaming channel; a syscall round trip on real hardware can be under 1 µs.
> 
> Recommendation: charge runtime in `time` ticks (the timebase), with a minimum of 1 tick per deschedule and the runtime capped at 2^40 ticks so the u64 step can't overflow. The step is ticks x STRIDE / weight. Weights are relative, so shares are unchanged; only the resolution improves. Timeouts and deadlines stay in µs as the ABI says.
> 
> The model keeps µs. Its differential test with the kernel's stride crate runs in one unit, and a model mutation R12ShortRunsFree shows the gaming would be caught.
> 
> Ask: approve ticks for charging, or require µs with carried remainders.

### Orchestrator · Answer

Event: `9c72158b41b9cf6e368db80405fc27b6` · 2026-09-24T17:54:19Z

> Approved: charge in timebase ticks, a minimum of 1 tick per deschedule, runtime capped at 2^40 ticks (2^40 x STRIDE 2^20 = 2^60 fits in u64). Timeouts and deadlines stay in µs per the ABI. One more hole, the same gaming channel one level down: weight is a u32 (up to 2^32) and STRIDE is 2^20, so ticks x STRIDE / weight floors to 0 for any weight above 2^20 x ticks. A large-weight budget (init, the steward, drivers, which get large manifest weights) running 1 tick and blocking is charged nothing. Fix it exactly: carry the division remainder per budget (rem = (rem + ticks x STRIDE) mod weight, step = the quotient), so charging is exact over time and never free. A floor of step >= 1 would overcharge large weights. Put the remainder in the overflow section (rem < weight <= u32 max, so the sum fits). Model: keep µs if its differential test against the kernel's stride crate runs in one unit, but the model must carry the remainder too. Extend R12ShortRunsFree, or add R12DropRemainder, and show that a large-weight short-burst spinner is caught. Add this to the K5 KERNEL-SPEC clarification commit: R12 charges in ticks with an exact remainder.

### Orchestrator · Resolved

Event: `7563e4fd0398cbe6edaa1202e80f0e41` · 2026-09-24T17:54:21Z

> Evidence: Charging in timebase ticks, min 1 tick per deschedule, runtime capped at 2^40 ticks (2^40 x STRIDE 2^20 fits in u64); timeouts and deadlines stay in µs. Added: carry the per-budget division remainder, because weight is up to u32 (KERNEL-SPEC budget table) and STRIDE is 2^20 (libs/sys/src/lib.rs:139), so large weights would otherwise be charged 0 for short bursts. The model carries the remainder, with a mutation. Goes into the K5 KERNEL-SPEC clarification commit; the owner confirms at plan approval.

> 
> Recommendation: K5 removes both legacy timer ops and adds no call. rdtime is for relative high-resolution timing; time_now is the unit-bearing clock. If a consumer needs the frequency, the INIT/R3 owner adds a startup-block field later (a spec change owned by the architect).
> 
> The alternative is to keep TIMER_TIMEBASE, open to everyone, until K6. That keeps an unspecified legacy call alive, so I don't recommend it.

## K5 · K5-q-icache — Kernel icache maintenance (R2-followups item 5): does K5 own the single-hart fence.i?

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 3

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

### K5 implementer · Question

Event: `79241425cfc345ef64dce1b3d3cc62cb` · 2026-09-24T17:52:34Z

> The kernel has no fence.i anywhere.
> - Single hart: a parent writes a child's code (process_map from spawn, or the loader stub via map_fixed), and nothing orders those stores before the child's first instruction fetch (Zifencei). The stub fences its own writes; nothing fences the parent's.
> - A physically tagged icache could also hold a previous owner's code in a recycled frame. That's a correctness hazard, not a privilege one: it runs in the new owner's context.
> - Multi-hart: migration needs a fence on the destination hart, or SBI remote fence.i.
> 
> Recommendation: K5 owns only the single-hart piece. One fence.i on the kernel path right before a newly started process's first thread first runs (process_start), in its own small commit: +1 unsafe asm in arch/riscv, with the ratchet updated honestly. The multi-hart piece stays with post-M1 SMP (PLAN, SMP). QEMU can't observe either, so the evidence is code review only; no bench case can show it.
> 
> Ask: yes (K5 owns the single-hart fence.i), or keep it out of K5 and schedule it elsewhere.

Before you settle on process_start as the only point, check the other ways a process can come to execute bytes it didn't fence itself, and cover each one or argue in the plan why it's safe:
> - process_map (or lend or transfer) into an already-started child with an executable mapping. If the kernel allows it, process_start alone isn't enough; fence when that mapping is installed, or on the next switch into that process.
> - set_flags flipping a page to executable, and map_fixed plus a later exec, done by the process on its own pages. The process is responsible (U-mode fence.i is unprivileged, as the stub does). Say so.
> - Recycled frames: say why a physically tagged stale line can't be executed without either the new owner's own write-then-fence, or one of the kernel paths above.

> K5 plan v1 red-team review. Read-only; code at wp-k5 08848f60a; wp-k5-unreviewed not inspected. Checked against WP-K5 acceptance, R10/R12/I13-I15, RESOURCES Scheduling/Timer, TENETS 3, answer 166 and the 7 resolved K5-q answers.
