> VERDICT: BLOCK. v2 must fix P1-1..P1-3 and should fold the P2s. P1-2 needs an orchestrator rule, because it narrows the approved K5-q-minimum answer that 'a new budget enters at the floor'.
> 
> P1-1 Charging choke point is incomplete; there is a free-CPU channel. The plan charges only in activate_process_thread, but several deschedules never pass through it:
> - thread_exit: destroy_thread -> switch_to_thread (services.rs:1852).
> - process_exit, faulted and a kill of the running process: end_process -> terminate_process -> switch_to_thread(parent) (process.rs:584, services.rs:2281).
> - finish_callback_and_resume and make_callback_to (services.rs:672/728).
> Attack: a user budget loops thread_create -> spin SLICE-e -> thread_exit, or does the same with child processes that exit or fault. No run is ever charged, so the budget's share is unbounded.
> Fix: account at the trap boundary. At every U-mode trap entry, charge (now - last return to U) to the budget of the process that ran (read before any teardown), or hook every current-(pid,tid) change including switch_to_thread. Add the boot attack case sched-exit-churn (thread churn plus process exit/fault churn; victim share >= w/W - tol) and a model mutation (e.g. R12ExitRunsFree).
> 
> P1-2 Budget churn sheds pass debt. A new budget enters at the floor, ranked as a waker (ahead of the queued budget at the minimum). Its first slice is charged to a budget that is then destroyed, and the carved weight returns to the parent.
> Attack: any holder of a user budget handle loops: budget_create(weight 1), spawn a spinner, let it run one full SLICE, budget_destroy, repeat. Each cycle costs a few syscalls plus an image copy and gains 10 ms. A weight-1 child takes about half the CPU from a weight-100 victim. That breaks 'a spinning budget cannot delay another beyond its weight' and RESOURCES 'always gets at least its share'.
> Pre-charging at creation is not enough: a pre-charge made at creation vanishes if the first wake comes after the floor has passed it (max(own, floor)), so budgets created early and started later get the free slice anyway.
> Options for the orchestrator:
> (a) Entry fee at the first wake: pass = floor + SLICE*STRIDE/weight.
> (b) Bill a destroyed budget's excess pass to the budget of its destroyer or creator. This is awkward for kernel-deadline destruction.
> (c) Other.
> Whatever the rule, add the sched-budget-churn boot case, create/destroy churn in the model fairness generator, and a mutation.
> 
> P1-3 Entry-time expiry kills or invalidates state the trap handler already captured (I14 panics):
> (a) kmain's own SwitchTo is a legacy ecall from PID 1 (main.rs:144). Expiry at that entry can destroy the picked process through a budget deadline, and then activate_process_thread fails at expect('couldn't switch to pid'), which panics.
> (b) trap_handler reads pid = current_pid() once (irq.rs:192) and uses it later for PREVIOUS_PAIR (irq.rs:290), redoubt::handle, syscall::handle and faulted. If expiry at entry kills the current process, all of those name a dead PID.
> Fix:
> - PID-1 entries never expire. kmain runs expire -> reconcile -> pick -> SwitchTo with nothing in between, and a failed SwitchTo re-picks instead of panicking.
> - At a U-mode entry, expire first, then re-read current. If the entering thread died, skip the syscall's work and resume current. For an IRQ entry, re-read after expiry before recording PREVIOUS_PAIR.
> - Write this per entry kind in v2: Redoubt, legacy, external IRQ, timer, RETURN_FROM_ISR, EXIT_THREAD, fault.
> 
> P2 and P3 follow in the next reply.

> - At creation, a new budget's pass = max(floor, its PARENT BUDGET's pass). Not the creator process's budget: the tree parent whose weight it carves (R7).
> - At destroy (budget_destroy, deadline, or revocation), the parent budget's pass = max(parent pass, child pass), so the child's unpaid debt moves up the tree and isn't dropped. Apply it bottom-up for a destroyed subtree, in R10 order.
> - A parent budget that holds no process never runs, so debt parked on it only raises the entry pass of its next children. The floor catches up over time; there is no permanent penalty.

> N1 (carve inflation): a budget's stride weight is its FREE weight (its weight limit minus what it has carved to children), not its limit. So carving moves share and never duplicates it (R7). > # WP-D3 plan v1: netd and ipd (the network)
> 
> Worktree `/home/mick/riscv/.worktrees/d3`, branch `wp-d3` at main `08848f60a`. PLAN ONLY: no code, no tracked-file edits, no commits. D3 does not touch `kernel/`, `model/` or `tests/programs/**`, and needs **no new kernel feature**. The kernel calls it uses (`send` with a transfer, `receive` with `max_transfer`, IRQ receive, `dma_alloc`, `map_device -> addr,len`, `thread_create`, `mint`, `process_*`, `map_fixed`) are all merged.
> 
> **Starting point.** SWARM lists D3 as "building / external claim unverified". No source exists: no `servers/netd` or `servers/ipd`, no network commits in any local or remote branch, and the recovery inventory says "no wp-d3 branch was among the four". This plan starts from scratch. Nothing external is merged.
> 
> ## OWNER DECISIONS (need confirmation before implementation)
> 
> Each item below is my recommendation. The ones marked [QA] also have their own spec-gap thread to the orchestrator.
> 
> 1. **smoltcp 0.14.0, pinned exactly (`=0.14.0`) with `default-features = false`.** Features: `alloc`, `medium-ethernet`, `proto-ipv4`, `socket-tcp`, and nothing else. That leaves out IPv6, DHCP, DNS, UDP, raw and ICMP sockets, IP fragmentation/reassembly, `auto-icmp-echo-reply` (no ping), `log`, `defmt`, `std` and the phy backends. Details and checks are in section 2.
> 2. **IPv4 only, static configuration, TCP only in D3.** `/net/udp` is deferred, which is a deliberate gap against NAMESPACES "/net/udp/... the same shape": milestone 1's SSH path needs none of it. The interface address and gateway come from ipd's arguments; there is no DHCP client. [QA D3-q-scope]
> 3. **Frames reach ipd as a `send` with a page transfer from netd, and ipd transmits with a `call` to netd.** This is the shape PLAN's attack suite already assumes ("ipd still receives netd's frames (sends)", answer 81). It makes D3 the first protocol that needs WIRE's anticipated **`kind` column** ("added when a protocol first needs a send"). That means an additive change to the generator `libs/wire/gen`, which W1/W2 own, and it changes WIRE's sentence "every milestone 1 typed message is a call". [QA D3-q-frames]
> 4. **Backpressure on `/net/tcp/N/data` writes.** NAMESPACES says "a waiting write remains a non-goal". Without one, a TCP sender with a full buffer can only busy-poll. The recommendation is a small additive `libs/rt` change, `FileServer::write -> Write::Wait`, parking exactly as `Read::Wait` does with the same admission and deadline. It needs a shared-runtime review round, like 157/163. The fallback, if refused, is a short Rwrite (at least 1 byte) and, when the buffer is completely full, an Rerror "busy" that the client retries after a parking ctl read that waits for "writable". [QA D3-q-write-wait]
> 5. **How the capability is represented (section 3).** Root scopes come from ipd's manifest arguments, one per root badge. Narrowing uses a typed `grant(scope)` (opcode 16 on ipd's 9P endpoint, WIRE's Granting rule); `ninep_common` `new_connection("")` gives a same-scope fresh connection, and `disconnect(id)` releases either kind. This needs a small additive `libs/rt` API so grant uses the skeleton's single `Minted` table (`NineServer::mint_rooted`). [QA D3-q-scope]
> 6. **"The box's own addresses" (section 3.4).** ipd always refuses, whatever the scope says: its own interface address(es), 127.0.0.0/8, 0.0.0.0/8, broadcast (limited and directed), 224.0.0.0/4, 240.0.0.0/4, and every `self=` prefix the manifest declares. On QEMU that is gateway 10.0.2.2/32, which reaches host loopback and so the forwarded ssh port. **Stated residual:** an address that routes back through NAT hairpinning somewhere outside the box is refused only if the manifest lists it. ipd cannot discover it. [QA D3-q-scope]
> 7. **/net file contents are typed encodings, not text.** This includes the ctl writes that WIRE already specifies, clone/ctl reads, and remote. Connect and listen completion is reported by a **parking read of ctl**, so no waiting write is needed for them. [QA D3-q-ctl]
> 8. **Evidence before R3.** A D3-owned test launcher (`tests/net`, the "rig") boots the real netd/ipd binaries through the real R2 stub, with named startup handles, on the real kernel and QEMU NIC. It is the evidence for TCP and the attack cases now. Manifest-driven boot through init stays a retained R3 / full-server gate, the same pattern as blkd's "boot integration waits". Orchestrator to confirm this is acceptable D3 acceptance evidence. [QA D3-q-bench]
> 9. **Bench: QEMU `virtio-mmio.force-legacy` defaults to on** (QEMU 10.2.2 here: "force-legacy default: on"). Both blkd and netd speak only virtio-mmio version 2, so **no real virtio driver can boot on the bench as configured**. That affects D2 as well. Fix: add `-global virtio-mmio.force-legacy=false` whenever a case has [disk] or [net], one line in qemu.rs. Do not add a legacy path to the drivers. [QA D3-q-bench]
> 10. **A device that lies makes netd refuse, not exit** (blkd's rule). netd resets the device (STATUS=0, which stops its DMA), then answers `failed` to every request.
> 11. **Stated residuals:**
>    - smoltcp's TCP initial sequence numbers come from one PCG32 seeded once from the kernel CSPRNG, so they are predictable after a few observations. That enables off-path injection on a hostile LAN, and one unlabelled user can observe another's connection rate. ipd picks ephemeral ports itself from `random`, so ports do not leak it.
>    - A NIC flood costs netd's weight-1000 CPU.
>    - Restart DMA hazard, Q147, same as blkd.
>    - A SYN flood can hold a listener's sockets in SYN-RECEIVED for up to its 10 s timeout.

> ## 1. netd: the virtio-net driver
> 
> **Crate `servers/netd`** (redoubt-netd; lib + bin netd; depends only on redoubt-rt). It mirrors blkd module for module, and IO-ARCHITECTURE's "netd inherits this decision" (our own queue, no virtio-drivers) applies. Files:
> 
> - `src/lib.rs`: the trust statement (what netd is trusted for, stated like blkd's three promises). `deny(unsafe_code)` everywhere except `kernel`.
> - `src/transport.rs`: the same `Transport` seam as blkd: reg read/write, DMA read/write, phys, len, wait_irq, now_us, fence. It is copied, not shared. Factoring a libs/virtio crate would reopen blkd's reviewed TCB, so that is a later follow-up.
> - `src/kernel.rs`: the only unsafe: volatile MMIO and DMA byte access, as blkd's four blocks. It refuses a register window shorter than CONFIG+8 (MAC plus status).
> - `src/virtio.rs`: register map (virtio 1.2 4.2.2), status handshake, net constants (5.1), DeviceError.
> - `src/rxq.rs` and `src/txq.rs`: two split virtqueues, each in **its own dma_alloc region** (below).
> - `src/device.rs`: bring-up and the two queue drivers. `src/server.rs`: the netif protocol.
> - `src/fake.rs` (host only): a hostile virtio-net device model.
> - `src/bin/netd.rs`: the two threads.
> - `tests/device.rs`, `tests/server.rs`; `fuzz/` (a cargo-fuzz crate excluded from the workspace, as servers/blkd/fuzz).
> 
> **Bring-up refuses rather than works around.**
> - The transport is version 2 only, and the device ID must be 1 (net).
> - Accept exactly VERSION_1 (32) and MAC (5); both are required, and a device without them is refused.
> - Everything else is left unaccepted: CSUM, GUEST_CSUM, all TSO/UFO, MRG_RXBUF, CTRL_VQ, STATUS, MQ, EVENT_IDX and INDIRECT_DESC. So the device may send no GSO, no merged buffers and no checksum offload.
> - FEATURES_OK must read back. MAC config is read under ConfigGeneration, retried at most 8 times.
> - QueueNumMax must be at least 16 for queue 0 (rx) and queue 1 (tx), otherwise refuse. Reset is polled a bounded number of times.
> 
> **The DMA layout. Nothing the device says is used as an index or a length.** There are two regions, each self-contained, and every address given to the device is region_phys + a constant (compile-time LAYOUT_FITS asserts, as blkd):
> 
> - **RX region** (rx thread): desc[16], avail, used, then 16 slots of 2048 B. Each slot takes the 12-byte virtio_net_hdr (v1 size) plus a frame up to 1514 B.
>   - Descriptor i always points at slot i with length 2048 and WRITE. The table and avail ring are written from constants and **never read back**.
> - **TX region** (serving thread): desc[16], avail (with NO_INTERRUPT), used, then 16 slots of 2048 B.
> 
> **What netd validates on the used ring** (read at netd's own counter, never at a device index):
> - idx advances by at most the number of outstanding buffers.
> - Each entry's id is < 16 and currently outstanding (an outstanding bitmap). A duplicate or an unknown id is a lie.
> - rx len is at least 12 and at most 2048. The header must say flags == 0 (no NEEDS_CSUM, since it was not negotiated) and gso_type == NONE.
> - The frame length is len - 12, between 14 and 1514.
> - The frame is copied out **once**, with netd's own length, before any byte is looked at.
> - tx len is ignored beyond the at-most check.
> 
> Anything else is broken (decision 10). A tx slot outstanding longer than **10 s** is also broken (blkd's timeout).
> 
> **Threads: no shared memory, no locks.** consoled's precedent is "no shared state between the two".
> - **Serving thread.** Owns the TX region and bring-up. It receives on `netd`:
>   - info and transmit from the client badge;
>   - the rx thread's one startup message, carrying the RX region's physical address in words;
>   - BROKEN from the rx thread.
> 
>   transmit works like this:
>   1. Reclaim validated tx used entries.
>   2. Take a free slot; if none, reply busy.
>   3. Write the header (zeros) and the frame into the slot.
>   4. Publish to avail and notify queue 1.
>   5. Reply.
> 
>   It never blocks on anything but its own receive.
> - **Rx thread.** Makes its own map_device and dma_alloc for the RX region, fills its rings and posts all 16 buffers. It then sends the region's physical address to the serving thread, which programs queue 0 and sets DRIVER_OK. Its loop:
>   1. wait_irq, read InterruptStatus and write InterruptACK.
>   2. Drain validated rx entries: copy each frame into a fresh 1-page Buffer, repost the slot.
>   3. send the frame to ipd, with a 50 ms timeout. On Timeout/Busy/Refused it drops the frame and reuses the buffer; drops are counted.
> 
>   It blocks only itself.
> - **Why this does not deadlock.** ipd (one thread) calls netd.transmit, and netd's serving thread always answers promptly. netd's rx thread may block in send to ipd, but that holds up nothing ipd waits for. No transfer is made within one process, so the open question 138 is not touched.
> 
> **Interface to ipd.** This is the IO-ARCHITECTURE "interface capability". Proposed tables: netif goes in IO-ARCHITECTURE's netd note (its own endpoint, opcodes from 1); frame goes in ipd's table (section 3).
> 
> ```
> [wire: netif]
> | Opcode | Message  | Fields         | Reply                  |
> | 1      | info     | -              | mac: u64, mtu: u32     |   (inline, 12 bytes)
> | 2      | transmit | frame: bytes   | -                      |   (buffer; lend 1 page)
> [wire-errors: netif]  2 not_permitted, 3 too_many (frame > 1514 or < 14), 4 busy (tx ring full), 5 failed (device broken)
> ```
> 
> - **Startup handles** (Q149 recommendation, NAME / NAME-irq): `netd` (receive right), `net` (MMIO with DMA), `net-irq`, and `ipd` (a send handle to ipd's endpoint with ipd's ingress badge).
> - **Argument:** `client=<badge>`, the only badge allowed info and transmit. Any other badge or a labelled caller gets not_permitted. A send to netd is dropped and its handles closed.
> - **Exit codes, as blkd:** NO_ENDPOINT, NO_DEVICE, NO_NIC, BAD_ARGS, RECEIVE_FAILED.
> - **netd's note** in IO-ARCHITECTURE Networking gets: what it is trusted for, bounds (16/16 slots, 1514 B, 10 s), each error's meaning, and the Q147 residual.

> ## 3. /net over 9P and the IP-prefix-and-port capability
> 
> ### 3.1 The tree (NAMESPACES "The network tree", made concrete)
> 
> ```
> /             the connection's root; its node carries the connection's scope id
> /tcp/         lists only THIS connection's sockets (no leaky state)
> /tcp/clone    read at offset 0 allocates socket N (charged) and returns N (u32)
> /tcp/N/ctl    Twrite: typed ops (3.2); Tread: status (u32 state), PARKS while connecting or listening
> /tcp/N/data   read: bytes, PARKS when empty (0 = peer closed); write: bytes (backpressure: decision 4)
> /tcp/N/remote read: addr: bytes[4], port: u16 (typed)
> ```
> 
> - **Why read-to-allocate instead of Plan 9's open-and-retarget.** The skeleton cannot move a fid's node on open, and a node holds no resource. So clone hands out N by read.
> - **Socket lifetime.** A socket lives until ctl close (graceful, freed after TIME-WAIT), abort, or disconnect of its connection (which aborts all of that connection's sockets). The admission charge bounds a sloppy client to its own bucket, and a launcher's disconnect on child exit reclaims everything (CONTAINMENT: disconnect frees a connection's state).
> - **Visibility.** A walk to another connection's N is "not found". FileServer::labels() is [] for every node.
> 
> ### 3.2 ctl operations
> 
> WIRE: one Twrite per op, the opcode as a u32, then the buffer-shaped fields. The table is proposed for NAMESPACES:
> 
> ```
> [wire: net_ctl]
> | 1 | connect | addr: bytes (4, IPv4, network order), port: u16 | - |
> | 2 | listen  | port: u16                                    | - |
> | 3 | close   | -                                            | - |
> | 4 | abort   | -                                            | - |
> [wire-errors: net_ctl] 2 not_permitted, 3 in_use, 4 too_many, 5 state, 6 unreachable, 7 refused, 8 timeout
> ```
> 
> - **Scope refusals are synchronous.** connect checks the self set, then the scope, then state, **before** smoltcp sees anything. A refusal is an Rerror naming the error. Success means the attempt started. The client then reads ctl, which parks until the socket is established or fails.
> - **Listen.** listen puts N into LISTEN on the interface address. Reading ctl parks until a peer connects, and then N is that connection (smoltcp semantics). For a backlog of K, the holder keeps K listening sockets.
>   - **Only one lineage may hold a port.** A port listened on by one root-badge lineage is in_use for any other, so "ipd:lan delivers port 22 only to sshd" holds even with several listen grants.
>   - Any remote may connect to a listener, since the spec scopes listen by port only.
> 
> ### 3.3 The capability: representation, granting, checking
> 
> - **Representation.** A Scope is at most 8 rules:
>   - Connect{prefix: IPv4 net + len, ports: lo..=hi}
>   - Listen{ports: lo..=hi}
> - **Wire compound** (WIRE's "compound values are a bytes field whose layout is stated"): count: u8, then per rule kind: u8 (1 connect, 2 listen), addr: bytes[4] (network order; 0 for listen), len: u8 (at most 32), lo: u16, hi: u16, with lo <= hi.
> - **Root scopes.** init mints ipd's badges from the manifest; ipd's scope= arguments say what each root badge means.
>   - Milestone-1 manifest: steward badge = c:0.0.0.0/0:1-65535; sshd badge = l:22; netd = the ingress badge, which has no /net.
>   - The manifest's per-principal net scope (INIT.md) is applied by the steward via grant.
> - **Granting.** Typed grant(scope: bytes) -> conn: handle[0] endpoint, id: u64 (ipd's ninep table, opcode 16). Every requested rule must lie inside one held rule: the same kind, prefix contained, port range contained. Anything wider is not_permitted, so a grant can never widen or add listen.
>   - It is minted through the skeleton's Minted table with the new root node carrying the scope (the mint_rooted addition), so it gets a random badge above 2^63, a random id, answer-168 rollback and admission State.
>   - new_connection("") gives the same scope (launchers); new_connection("tcp") also keeps the scope.
> - **Release.** ninep_common disconnect(id) frees that connection, everything minted under it, and aborts their sockets. Only the id's holder may name it (not_yours).
> - **Checking.** On every connect(addr, port):
>   1. addr in the self set: not_permitted, whatever the scope (decision 6).
>   2. Otherwise at least one Connect rule must contain (addr, port).
> 
>   On listen(p): a Listen rule must contain p, and the lineage rule holds (3.2).
> 
> ```
> [wire: ipd ninep]
> | Opcode | Kind | Message | Fields        | Reply                               |
> | 16     | call | grant   | scope: bytes  | conn: handle[0] endpoint, id: u64   |
> | 17     | send | frame   | frame: bytes  | -                                   |   (ingress badge only; 1-page transfer)
> [wire-errors: ipd] 2 not_permitted, 3 too_many
> ```
> 
> ### 3.4 The self set
> 
> **Never includes the box's own addresses, loopback included.** It holds:
> - addr's host address, the network and directed-broadcast addresses of addr/len, and 255.255.255.255;
> - 127.0.0.0/8 and 0.0.0.0/8;
> - 224.0.0.0/4 and 240.0.0.0/4 (not unicast);
> - every self= argument. On QEMU the manifest names 10.0.2.2/32: slirp maps the gateway to host loopback, where hostfwd leads back to the guest's port 22. That is the CAPABILITIES "loopback login" route.
> 
> The check runs **before** the scope check, so a manifest that wrongly scoped 0.0.0.0/0 still cannot reach the box. The check sits in scope.rs and is one function, covered by a table test.
> 
> ## 4. Confinement
> 
> - **One ipd per network or trust domain.** ipd keeps no statics and no cross-instance state. Its whole configuration is its arguments and handles, so two instances are two processes with two budgets. netd pushes to exactly one ipd, so a second trust domain on one NIC needs a second NIC/netd pair or linkd (Later).
> - **The manifest side is R3's.** init refuses a confined manifest in which differing label sets share an ipd:* / netd. That is WP-R3's refusal, not D3's.
> - **A labelled domain gets no /net.** The steward and manifest give it none (S2/R3). **ipd refuses labelled callers regardless.**
>   - The check runs at the top of the loop, before 9P, ninep_common, grant or admission, on every call and send, keyed by kernel-attached caller.labels, which cannot be forged.
>   - So a labelled budget that obtained an ipd handle anyway gets not_permitted / Rerror on everything and never opens a bucket (CONTAINMENT: sinks are cleared for nothing).
> - **netd** accepts only its configured client badge and unlabelled callers.
> 
> ## 5. Resource accounting and DoS
> 
> **ipd admission** (libs/rt Admission, per (account, label set); account 0 per badge):
> - Limits: buckets 8, in_flight 5 (8 x 5 = 40, which is at most MAX_OPEN_CALLS - OPEN_CALL_HEADROOM = 48), files 24 (fids), state 16 (minted connections plus sockets, charged as Resource::State through admission_mut()).
> - sshd's bucket (a system caller, per badge) needs about 4 listening sockets plus one per session, which fits in 16.
> - Every bucket at its cap must fit ipd's budget (Limits::fits):
>   - Socket buffers are 8 KiB rx + 8 KiB tx, so 8 x 16 x 16 KiB = 2 MiB.
>   - Parked lends are up to 16 pages each: 40 x 68 KiB, about 2.7 MiB.
>   - Plus about 1 MiB of heap and smoltcp.
>   - Proposed ipd budget: 8 MiB.
> 
> **Parked calls:**
> - A ctl read waiting to connect or accept has a **60 s** server deadline. A data read has **30 s** and then answers Rerror "timeout"; the client re-reads. It waits on the network, not a person, so it is not the console's FOREVER exception.
> - Abandoned calls are answered at once.
> - The serve before resuming comes from Parked.
> 
> **What a hostile caller can exhaust:** only its own bucket (and its share inside it), plus the stated shared cap of 8 bucket slots.
> - Handles a request brings are closed.
> - Client sends are dropped and their transfer unmapped; max_transfer = 1, and larger transfers are Refused by the kernel.
> - The work of one request is bounded to at most one msize copy and one socket operation.
> - **The pinned-open-calls attack.** Bob parks 64 calls and gets 5 parked, the rest refused. Even at MAX_OPEN_CALLS, R4a still delivers sends, so netd's frames and abandonment notices keep arriving.
> 
> **What a hostile network peer can exhaust:**
> - A listener's sockets. A SYN flood holds them in SYN-RECEIVED until a 10 s timeout, which is the stated residual; the backlog is K sockets.
> - A connection's own 8 KiB buffers.
> - smoltcp's fixed neighbor cache, route table and reassembly assembler, which are sized at compile time. IP fragments are dropped, since reassembly is off.
> - ipd CPU per frame, at ipd's ordinary weight.
> - netd CPU at weight 1000 (stated residual).
> - One page per frame in transit. If ipd's budget is short, the kernel says Refused and the frame is dropped.
> 
> There is no unbounded queue anywhere:
> - The device holds at most 16 rx buffers.
> - netd has one send in flight.
> - ipd has a one-frame rx slot, consumed by poll straight away.
> - netd's tx ring answers busy, and smoltcp retransmits.
> 
> **netd:** one client badge; transmit is bounded (1514 B) and never parks; 16 + 16 slots.

Event: `f3989b652076c8648115f0b1a2434dec` · 2026-09-24T20:21:24Z

> The rulings are recorded in the plan file (a "Rulings received" section at the top). Write::Wait will be **general** in libs/rt: any FileServer may return it, and in M1 only /net data does. The NAMESPACES amendment will say exactly that. v2 will fold in the red team's findings when they arrive. Still PLAN ONLY.
> 
> **Decision 11: mitigation, no fork.**
> 
> **What smoltcp 0.14 offers.** No direct hook. Its Rand is pub(crate), and the seed exists only as Config::random_seed at Interface::new. The ISN comes from cx.rand() in two places: tcp::Socket::connect(cx, ..) for active opens (tcp.rs:1063), and SYN processing in ingress for passive opens (tcp.rs:1919).
> 
> **The public API is enough.** Sockets live in the SocketSet, apart from the Interface. And connect takes any &mut Context (Interface::context() is public).
> 
> So:
> 1. **Active open.** ipd builds a throwaway Interface with random_seed = the kernel CSPRNG's random_u64(). It has the same hardware address, IP address and default route, and uses a null device. ipd calls socket.connect(fresh.context(), ..) on it, with the local port also from `random`.
> 2. **Passive open.** ipd parses its one-frame rx slot with smoltcp::wire. If the frame is IPv4 TCP with SYN and no ACK addressed to ipd, it is processed with fresh.poll_ingress_single(now, link, sockets) on a freshly seeded throwaway. The SYN-ACK leaves later through the main interface's egress. Every other frame goes through the main interface.
> 
> So the main interface's PRNG never produces an ISN. One helper builds both interfaces from the same arguments, so their configurations cannot drift.
> 
> **What each ISN is.** PCG32 output #2 of an independent 64-bit CSPRNG seed.
> - Output #1 seeds ipv4_id, which is never emitted: with fragmentation off, wire/ipv4.rs:604 always emits ident 0.
> - TCP timestamps stay off (tsval_generator None).
> - Cost: one `random` syscall and one small Interface::new per connect or SYN. That is bounded per frame, SYN flood included.
> 
> **Tests.** An injected seed source checks that:
> - each connect or accepted SYN consumes exactly one seed;
> - the ISN of connection k equals output 2 of seed k;
> - none of 1000 ISNs appears among the first 10k outputs of the main interface's seed (a mutation guard).
> 
> **Residual, stated precisely.**
> - **Blind off-path injection.** The attacker must guess an in-window sequence number: with an 8 KiB window, about 2^19 tries per connection, the same as any random-ISN stack. The worst case is a reset, or injected bytes that SSH's transport MAC rejects, which ends the session. That is a denial of service, not a compromise.
> - **Cross-user connection-rate channel.** The shared observable PRNG is gone. Ports come from `random`, and no IP-ID counter is emitted. What remains between **unlabelled** users sharing one ipd are admission-slot occupancy and CPU/queue timing, which CONTAINMENT already states. No label boundary is involved, since labelled callers are refused.

>   - Proposed kernel fix after K5: quarantine a device's dma_alloc frames until the kernel resets it (STATUS=0, then a poll), done when the last allocating process dies or the handle is released.

Event: `f15ef1aff4aa11318ae63ec5242446d8` · 2026-09-24T23:11:27Z

> Defensive change for netd, from K5 review 5: on QEMU virt, an interrupt raised while the IRQ object is masked (between receives) was lost once, on a driver's FIRST receive. No kernel defect was found, and it's being followed up with K3. Make netd robust to a missed interrupt: after every IRQ receive returns (and once right after DRIVER_OK, before the first receive), drain the used rings until empty, and re-check the used ring index before blocking again, so a lost first edge can't stall rx or tx. Add a host test where the fake device completes a buffer without raising the interrupt, before the first receive, and netd still delivers it. Include it in checkpoint (c).

> - Fold at the old weight before a carve (add_budget) and before a return (destroy_budget), then rem rescaled and min(new-1).
> - The floor is monotone, raised at every fold, deschedule and reconcile, and held while the queue is empty.
> - Rank: wakes take front-1 in descending id; every runnable deschedule takes back+1; both reset when the queue empties.
> - Exact remainder charging, with the cap.
> - Entry e is stored. Lift = max(pass, f) + ((pass - max(e, f))+ x w_c + rem) / w_p, with the carry.
> - Boot is 1,000,000 / 250,000 / 749,000. Root keeps 1000 free and init stays in root; the boot check still passes.
> - Timeouts only wake; a budget deadline preempts; the equal-instant order is timeouts first.
> 
> MUTATIONS: each of the 19 is caught, and for a legitimate reason (the --nocapture output names the property). I also checked the intended scenario on its own, by seed residue. Detected:
> - gaming (d): DropRemainder (first at seed 1351) and ShortRunsFree (seed 21);
> - debt lift (i): UnnormalizedLift (seed 6);
> - churn (g): LiftByMax;
> - carve (h): StrideWeightIsLimit;
> - idempotence (l): FoldAtNewWeight;
> - sched_contracts: R7CarveToZeroFree and ProcessInWeightlessBudget (the free-weight invariant), TimeoutWakePreempts, PreemptOnWake, ExpireBudgetsFirst, BudgetDeadlineIgnored;
> - ipc_contracts: TimeoutIgnoredWhileOthersRun (I13).
> 
> DIFFERENTIAL: meaningful. The crate's rules are written independently of the model's (separate code; the queue is slot-based and the model is BTreeMap-based), and the comparison runs after every step on pass, entry, rem, tie, queued, floor, the counters and current. I planted 8 bugs in the crate (lift by max, ascending wake order, no rescale, requeue at the front, no floor raise at a fold, lift measured from f, no counter reset, rem dropped in the lift). The differential caught every one on the first failing seed.
> 
> DEBT-LIFT BOUND (K5-debt-lift-bound): the analysis is right. Equal-weight spinners sit at f or f + step, so S at f + epsilon ranks behind those at f and ahead of those at f + step, which is at most one round (N + 2 slices). R12UnnormalizedLift is caught decisively: S never runs within the 1000-slice cap (waited 10,000,000 µs against a bound of (n+3) x 10,000).
> 
> P2-1 The shell scenario (k) does NOT catch R12LiftCountsEntryWait: 0 of 3000 shell seeds (residue 9). Only idempotence (j) catches it. The shell's children are created when P usually has little lead, and the floor decays that lead between commands, so the geometric growth never appears. That matters for commit 5: the boot case sched-budget-churn (e) copies this shape. A kernel wiring bug that fails to persist entry (the frame word reading 0 makes the lift measure from f, which is exactly this mutation) would pass the boot bench. Strengthen (k), and the boot variant: have P create and destroy several heavy children back-to-back inside its own slice (tiny or no runs, P holding a lead). It should then fail under the mutation.
> 
> P2-2 Property (b) is vacuous in sched_rank. Every '_' iteration runs the slice to its end, so s.current is None whenever a wake (case 0) happens, and the 'a wake preempted' check never has a running thread. R12PreemptOnWake is caught only by sched_contracts' single timeout example (0 of 3000 rank seeds). Let wakes happen mid-slice: run part of a slice, wake, then check current is unchanged.
> 
> P2-3 DECISION 5's 'at least 1 tick per deschedule' is in neither the crate nor the model. charge() with runtime 0 charges nothing. Decide where it lives, the crate's fold or the kernel's trap-boundary accounting, and test it there. Otherwise a U-mode burst shorter than one tick (100 ns on QEMU's 10 MHz timebase) is free. If it goes in the crate, the model needs the matching floor (or the differential feeds max(1) to both).
> 
> P2-4 The differential's 'Kernel' is a harness written like the model (the same cursor, pending and deschedule code), not the kernel's future sched.rs. At commit 5, drive the kernel's actual wiring through this differential (e.g. put the wiring in a module both use), or it only proves crate = model.
> 
> P3:
> 1. lift: child.pass.saturating_sub(from) * w_child is an unchecked u128 multiply, and charge's rem + runtime x STRIDE assumes weight < 2^32 while the Budgets trait returns u64. Both are unreachable today, but checked builds would panic (I14). Use saturating_mul, and debug_assert or clamp weight <= u32::MAX.
> 2. Queue::reconcile loops forever if insert() finds no free slot (contains() stays false). That can't happen while runnable <= N, but a broken invariant would hang the kernel with SIE clear instead of failing. Break or assert when an insert fails.
> 3. The differential never destroys the running budget directly (its threads always exit first) and never a multi-level subtree in one operation (all threads ended, then bottom-up lifts with floor raises between). The kernel's deadline path does both; add those shapes.
> 4. DropRemainder is weakly caught by gaming (d) (only 1 of about 135 gaming seeds); the exact check in (l) carries it. That is fine, but (d)'s large-weight branch could burst smaller to bite more often.

## D3 · D3-q-ctl — D3: /net ctl/clone/remote encodings, completion signalling, deadlines, socket lifetime

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 2

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

### D3 implementer · Question

Event: `c91414ade070eba6f67db0fc172e901e` · 2026-09-24T20:18:42Z

> **Spec.**
> - NAMESPACES /net: clone, N/ctl ("typed connect/listen/close operations (WIRE.md)"), N/data, N/remote.
> - WIRE: a ctl op is one Twrite, a u32 opcode then buffer-encoded fields.
> 
> **Unspecified**, with my recommendation for each:
> 
> 1. **The table.** `net_ctl`: `1 connect(addr: bytes[4] network order, port: u16)`, `2 listen(port: u16)`, `3 close`, `4 abort`. Errors: 2 not_permitted, 3 in_use, 4 too_many, 5 state, 6 unreachable, 7 refused, 8 timeout. They surface as a 9P Rerror whose ename is the error name.
> 2. **Completion.**
>    - Connect and listen return once the attempt has started. Scope and self-address refusals are synchronous.
>    - A read of ctl parks until the state leaves connecting, or for a listener until a peer arrives, and returns a typed `state: u32`. So no waiting write is needed.
>    - For a listen backlog of K, hold K listening sockets.
> 3. **clone.** The skeleton cannot retarget a fid on open, and nodes hold no resource. So reading tcp/clone at offset 0 allocates socket N, charged to the caller's bucket, and returns `N: u32`.
> 4. **remote** returns a typed `addr: bytes[4], port: u16`. All /net contents are typed; there is no text.
> 5. **Lifetime.** A socket is freed by ctl close (after TIME-WAIT), by abort, or by disconnect of its connection (not by clunk). /net/tcp lists only the caller's connection's sockets.
> 6. **Parked deadlines.** A ctl wait is 60 s. A data read is 30 s, then Rerror timeout; it waits on the network, so it is not console's FOREVER exception.
> 7. **UDP** (/net/udp) is deferred out of D3.
> 
> **Decision needed.** Approve these, or amend. The tables then go into NAMESPACES with an ANSWERS record.

## D3 · D3-q-write-wait — D3: TCP write backpressure vs NAMESPACES 'a waiting write remains a non-goal'

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 2

*Resolved in an earlier workspace; reopen it if the code has changed since.*

### D3 implementer · Question

Event: `f703004b5811c4145de2625fdf4bde44` · 2026-09-24T20:18:42Z

> **Spec.** NAMESPACES, Holding a call: "Among 9P file operations, only read waits in milestone 1 ... A waiting write remains a non-goal."
> 
> **Problem.**
> - A write to /net/tcp/N/data when the socket's tx buffer is full cannot park.
> - An Rwrite of 0 looks like a stall, and short writes with nothing accepted leave the client busy-polling.
> - sshd and beamlet's gen_tcp both write through this path.
> 
> **Recommendation.**
> - An additive libs/rt change: FileServer::write may return Write::Wait, handed back by serve_parking exactly like Read::Wait.
> - It is charged to the same Admission and has a server-side deadline (30 s, then Rerror timeout). An abandoned write is freed at once.
> - It gets a small shared-runtime review round, like 157/163, and does not overlap Q163's typed parking.
> 
> **Fallback, if refused.**
> - ipd accepts a partial write of at least 1 byte.
> - When the buffer is completely full it answers Rerror busy. The client then does a parking ctl read that waits for writable.
> 
> **Decision needed.** Approve Write::Wait (NAMESPACES and ANSWERS edit), or the fallback.

> 1. **Root scopes.** init mints ipd's badges, and ipd's arguments (server-defined, like keyd's name,purpose,seed) say what each root badge means: `scope=<badge>:c:0.0.0.0/0:1-65535` for the steward and `scope=<badge>:l:22` for sshd. `ingress=<badge>` marks netd's frame badge, which has no /net. > 2. **Narrowing.**
>    - A typed `grant(scope: bytes) -> conn: handle[0] endpoint, id: u64`, opcode 16 in ipd's ninep table. Each rule must lie inside a held rule, so it can never widen or add listen.
>    - Release is ninep_common disconnect(id), which covers descendants and aborts their sockets.
>    - new_connection("") keeps the same scope.
>    - It needs a small additive libs/rt API, NineServer::mint_rooted, so grant and new_connection share one Minted table.

>    - the interface address, network and directed broadcast, 255.255.255.255;
>    - 127/8 and 0/8;
>    - 224/4 and 240/4;
>    - every manifest `self=` prefix. On QEMU that is 10.0.2.2/32: slirp maps it to host loopback, and hostfwd leads it back to guest :22.
> 
>    Stated residual: routes-back addresses outside the box (NAT hairpin) are refused only if listed.
> 5. **Listen ports** are held per root-badge lineage; another lineage gets in_use. Any remote may connect to a listener.
> 6. **IPv4 and TCP only** in D3.
> 
> **Decision needed.** Approve, or amend. The text goes to NAMESPACES/INIT with an ANSWERS record.

Event: `d0cb03a84e1c104c582d9867a502df8c` · 2026-09-24T20:28:02Z

> Red-team code review, checkpoint 2: 2f5762b2e and ce95d19ba. Code reading in a scratch worktree at ce95d19ba, now removed. I did not re-run the boot cases; the implementer reports all PASS on rv64 and rv32.
> 
> VERDICT: BLOCK for merge on P1-1 (a small fix; commit 5 work can continue). Everything else is OK with notes.
> 
> P1-1 Budget-deadline deferral is keyed on PREVIOUS_PAIR, which the legacy ReturnToParent call sets outside any callback.
> - time.rs defers budget deadlines while arch::irq::in_callback(), which is PREVIOUS_PAIR.is_some() (irq.rs:88).
> - The legacy SysCall::ReturnToParent handler (syscall.rs:1040) calls set_isr_return_pair whenever SWITCHTO_CALLER is Some, which it normally is for any process kmain switched to. The legacy interface is served to every U-mode process, Redoubt-created ones included, with no gating, and nothing clears the pair without a real interrupt (finish_isr returns early unless HANDLING_IRQ).
> - By code reading, any process can therefore put the kernel into 'callback' mode indefinitely. Every budget deadline in the system is deferred (rearm arms only timeouts), so WP-K5's 'a deadline destroys its budget' is defeated, including for the caller's own lease.
> - Two pre-existing effects of the same state make it worse: redoubt::handle's in_irq makes every Redoubt call NotPermitted for every process (so the steward's budget_destroy is refused too: TENETS 3), and a later legacy Yield hits do_yield's expect on SWITCHTO_CALLER (a kernel panic, I14).
> Fix, in K5 since it owns the kernel:
> (a) key the deferral, and redoubt's in_irq, on the real callback state (HANDLING_IRQ, set only when the kernel starts a callback), not on PREVIOUS_PAIR;
> (b) refuse ReturnToParent from user processes (the SWITCHTO_CALLER comment says the mechanism is unused), or remove it with the other dead Xous scheduling calls.
> Add an attack case asserting that a process which makes the legacy call is still destroyed at its lease deadline, and that Redoubt calls keep working for everyone else.
> 
> Verified OK:
> - Entry protocol. Every trap except CallFromSMode (kmain's SwitchTo) expires first, then re-reads current: if the entering pid changed or its slot is free, it resumes current. PREVIOUS_PAIR, the syscall paths and faulted() all run after that check, so none sees a dead pid. kmain expires, picks and switches with no entry in between, a failed SwitchTo resets SWITCHTO_CALLER and re-picks, and its expect is gone. Idle-window S-mode timer and IRQ entries expire with running() = None. The SupervisorTimerInterrupt branch only rearms.
> - Deadline list integrity. Word 15 was unused before (checked at 7aedd10d6). new_budget writes it as None, then links; the budget_create failure path unlinks before freeing. destroy_marked unlinks each dying frame before freeing it, in ascending frame order, and the predecessor walk only ever touches live or not-yet-freed frames, so it is correct for head, middle and chains of dying nodes. No other path frees a budget frame. A descendant destroyed with its ancestor is gone from the list before its own deadline is looked up.
> - Order. Timeouts come before budgets at an equal instant (td <= bd); budgets by (deadline, id); timeouts by (deadline, then walk order (pid, tid)). now is fixed per call, so work per entry is bounded, and anything later is re-armed (an immediate interrupt if already past).
> - The deadline path's caller is running() (none for PID 1). destroy_subtree kills it last and returns caller_doomed, and a process killed through budgets_dying (its object charged to the subtree) is caught by the trap's re-read.
> - Arithmetic on both widths: us_to_ticks rounds up (frac x hz < 2^52, checked secs x hz), ticks_to_us floors and saturates, and set() adds BOOT_TICKS with a checked add. Boot fails closed without Time.
> - IRQ 0: interrupt_claim(0) is InterruptNotFound, the timer ops return UnhandledSyscall, irq-attack asserts both, and timer, timer-test and the constants are gone.
> - The icount option is purely additive (Option, default None; adds '-icount <s> -rtc clock=vm' only when set), so existing cases are unchanged.
> 
> Reply race (implementer's item 2): acceptable, and it matches the IPC completion row 'taken call times out: Later discarded, mask 0'. A reply entering after the timeout finds F_WAITING clear, gets discarded and closes the call, and the owed notice goes with it. That is pre-existing semantics (the caller-death race behaves the same way); the timer only makes it reachable without a second process. But I15 says 'reported ... exactly once'. P3: have the K5 docs commit state that when the reply wins the race, the discarded result is the report and no notice follows, so I15 and the model read the same.
> 
> finish_isr's expect (item 3): sound once P1-1 is fixed. With deferral keyed on a real callback, nothing kills the previous pair during one: Redoubt calls are refused in_irq, legacy calls are limited to can_call_from_interrupt, and timeouts only wake. As it stands, P1-1's stale pair (pid 1) is the one way in.
> 
> R10 cost (item 1): the relative assertion (lateness <= a hand destroy of the same shape + 1 ms) is sound for what it tests, timer latency. Two notes:
> (a) About 21 ms of virtual time per destroy is non-preemptible kernel time (SIE clear). It delays every interrupt and timeout on the machine, and it will show up directly in sched-latency's driver-wake p99/max whenever a lease ends. Record destroy duration as its own column in the latency table and set the target knowing it.
> (b) The cost scales with object frames (mark_dying and destroy_marked scan 0..high_frame; budgets_dying's find-from-0 loops are O(E x F)), which any budget can grow with its pages, so it inflates everyone's destroys. Yes, make it a tracked follow-up (per-subtree indexes for budgets and endpoints), not K5.
> 
> P3:
> 1. Deferred budget deadlines are re-armed only on the RETURN_FROM_ISR path. A callback that ends through EXIT_THREAD or a fault calls finish_isr without expiring or rearming, so a due deadline waits for the next entry. Call rearm (or expire) after every finish_isr.
> 2. Budget deferral during a genuine callback is unbounded: a callback that never returns holds every deadline, not only the CPU. It is the stated residual until K6, but state it as 'all deadlines', and note that grants are keyed by PID (grants.rs), so check that a Redoubt-created process that reuses a granted boot process's PID cannot inherit its legacy IRQ grant.
> 3. all-together now runs no program that arms the timer (log-server and ipc-client never block with a timeout), so it no longer covers timer/IPC interference under smp 1/2. Add a sleeper to it.
> 4. expire_due walks every thread once per due timeout (O(k x T) per entry), not the one shared walk the plan describes. That is fine for now; revisit with commit 5's billing.
> 5. Read sstatus.SPP before expire_at_entry rather than after. Nothing in expiry changes it today, but the check depends on that.

> Red-team review of D3 plan v1 (plan file wash-inbox-1-message-binary-scott.md) with the orchestrator's rulings on D3-plan. Scope is clean: no kernel/, model/ or tests/programs/**, and the testbench overlap with K5 stays within the ruling.

> VERDICT: BLOCK until v2 fixes P1-1 to P1-6. Every fix is a plan change with no new kernel feature. The P2 items are notes for v2.
> 
> == P1 ==
> P1-1 The bench peer does not count guest connections. The QEMU man page (-netdev user, guestfwd) says a chardev guestfwd `tcp:...-tcp:127.0.0.1:P` is opened at boot and 'used throughout QEMU's lifetime'. So the host peer sees one connection per forward at startup, whether the guest ever connects or connects many times. Consequences: `10.0.2.101:7 = 0` fails, or counts nothing real; `10.0.2.100 = 1` passes even if the guest never connected; the 'reaches nothing else' self-check and every attack verdict built on counts are not evidence. Fix: use the `guestfwd=tcp:ADDR:PORT-cmd:<helper>` form, which spawns a process per guest connection. The helper can be a testbench subcommand that echoes and reports to the bench. Add a must_fail twin in which the guest connects twice and the case expects 1, which proves the count really counts connections. This also removes the free_ports TOCTOU on the peer ports.
> 
> P1-2 The own-address boot sub-cases pass vacuously, so they catch no regression. With restrict=on, slirp drops every guest SYN except guestfwd matches, so 10.0.2.2:<hostfwd port>, 127.0.0.1 and 127.1.2.3 record 0 whether or not ipd checks. For 10.0.2.15 smoltcp ARPs for its own address and nobody answers. Fix: (a) give the rig's ipd `self=10.0.2.102/32` and guestfwd 10.0.2.102:7 to a counting helper, so a wide-scope attacker's connect must count 0, and a regression in self= or in 'self before scope' shows up as 1; (b) make the host end-to-end test the regression evidence: its link records every frame ipd emits and asserts no IPv4 destination in the self set and no ARP for a self address, under a 0.0.0.0/0 scope; (c) state in the plan which boot sub-cases are vacuous on slirp by construction.
> 
> P1-3 The QEMU self set is too narrow (3.4 and decision 6). libslirp sotranslate_out maps every address in the virtual network (10.0.2.0/24), except the DNS alias, to host loopback. It maps 10.0.2.3 to the host's resolver, often 127.0.0.53. Any non-vnet 127/8 or host address reaches the host directly. With restrict=off, each of those reaches the hostfwd back to the guest's sshd. The repo always sets restrict=on and binds hostfwd to 127.0.0.1, which closes this today; the gap is the manifest, which says `self=10.0.2.2/32`. Fix: the milestone QEMU manifest declares `self=10.0.2.0/24`, the bench rig uses its own narrower self= with the peers outside it, and the plan states that restrict=on is what closes slirp on the bench. Also state that the NAT-hairpin residual rests on sshd refusing keyd-held keys (CAPABILITIES; S3/E1), and that each ipd's self= must list every address of every ipd on the box (a follow-up for R3).
> 
> P1-4 The rx thread sends a physical address by message (section 1, 'the rx thread's one startup message, carrying the RX region's physical address'). The plan doesn't say how the serving thread authenticates it. consoled uses a fixed WAKE_BADGE=1. If netd copies that pattern and init mints a client handle with a colliding badge, the client can make netd program queue 0 with any physical address, and the device then DMAs network-controlled bytes anywhere in RAM. Fix: send no physical address at all. The serving thread dma_allocs both regions before thread_create and passes the rx region through an atomic written before the thread exists (consoled's WAKE_ENDPOINT precedent). BROKEN should arrive on a badge drawn from `random` above 2^63; netd must refuse `client=` equal to it; and nothing on that badge is accepted after DRIVER_OK except BROKEN.
> 
> P1-5 One packet from the network bricks the NIC. Section 1 treats a frame under 14 or over 1514 bytes as a device lie, which marks the device broken for good. On a tap or real LAN, an honest device delivers a peer's 1518-byte 802.1Q frame or a runt frame. Fix: distinguish a device lie (len > 2048, a bad or duplicate id, an idx jump, header flags or gso_type nonzero) from content netd doesn't accept (a frame length outside 14..1514 but within the buffer). The second case drops the frame and counts it, and the fuzz asserts that such a frame is not broken. Check num_buffers on QEMU before making any check on it strict.
> 
> P1-6 Q147 is understated for netd ('same as blkd'). blkd's device is idle between requests. netd always has 16 rx buffers posted, so after any netd death the next packet from the network is DMA'd into frames already returned to the pool: remote-controlled bytes in another process's (or the kernel's) memory. This needs the orchestrator to escalate Q147 (the kernel's reset-on-free recommendation) before netd restart or R3 use. Until then netd must reset the device (STATUS=0, then poll for 0) on every exit it controls and never free DMA regions while live. The residual is stated as a network-attacker write, not a device fault.
> 
> == P2 ==
> P2-1 TX stale-byte leak. The TX descriptor length is not specified. If it is a constant 2048, like the rx descriptors, the device sends trailing bytes of a previous frame to a new destination: Alice's traffic to A leaks to Bob's server B. The TX descriptor must be written for each transmit with len 12 + frame_len, and a host test should check the wire length.
> P2-2 ISN mitigation (the orchestrator asked for it). smoltcp can't be reseeded: Rand and InterfaceInner::rand are pub(crate), and random_seq_no is cx.rand().rand_u32(). PCG32 state is recoverable from one or two observed ISNs. Fork-free fix for outbound connections: Socket::connect(cx, remote, local) takes the Context, and with an explicit local address uses cx only for the ISN (tcp.rs:1013-1066). So ipd can pass the context() of a throwaway Interface::new(Config{random_seed: fresh kernel random}) for each connect, which makes outbound ISNs CSPRNG. Accepts still draw from the main Interface (tcp.rs:1919). Either rebuild the Interface with a fresh seed after each accept (the cost is re-ARPing the gateway) or state the residual precisely: listener ISNs are predictable, so an off-path attacker can complete a spoofed-source handshake (nothing trusts source IPs) or inject a reset or garbage, which SSH's MAC rejects (a DoS, not a compromise). A remote peer can also count the box-wide accept rate, a 'no global counters' channel among unlabelled users. Keep proto-ipv4-fragmentation off: the per-packet IPv4 ID counter exists only with it (ipv4.rs:33).
> P2-3 Crash blame. A thread's current call stays set while a call is parked or resumed; only a reply or a non-call receive clears it (KERNEL-SPEC current call). A smoltcp panic in the top-of-loop poll then blames the user whose read is parked, so three remote-triggered crashes destroy an innocent principal's budgets. Rule: run iface.poll only when the thread has no current call, which means ordering the loop so that a receive returning Timeout, Send or an abandoned notice precedes each poll. Test it on the host.
> P2-4 The labelled refusal is the only barrier to reads. The skeleton's check lets a caller labelled {7} read [] nodes ([] ⊆ {7}), which includes clone's read-to-allocate. So the refusal must live in a lib dispatch function that both the bin and the host tests use, not in bin/ipd.rs.
> P2-5 'Opens no bucket' is checked by an unchanged socket count from a control client, but 3.1 makes other connections' sockets invisible. Use bucket-slot exhaustion instead: buckets=K, the labelled attempt runs, then K distinct unlabelled accounts must all succeed. Give every attack case a positive control in the same boot (the victim accepts exactly one bench dial; an unlabelled twin with the same scope reaches the peer) and a distinct peer address per attacker, so counts can be attributed.
> P2-6 The listen-lineage rule is too coarse. The steward's root lineage covers every principal, so two principals granted the same port share it, and smoltcp hands a SYN to the first matching LISTEN socket (hijack). Key port ownership to the connection that first listened, plus its new_connection("") clones.
> P2-7 SYN flood. smoltcp's timeout moves SYN-RECEIVED to Closed, not back to LISTEN (tcp.rs:2470; only an RST re-listens, tcp.rs:1887), and with no timeout set, SYN-ACK retransmits forever. So ipd must set the timeout and re-listen by itself, without failing the holder's ctl read. Otherwise K spoofed SYNs every 10 s take sshd down. Consider 3 s and a larger K for sshd.
> P2-8 Socket numbers and ports. N must be per connection, not a global counter. Ephemeral ports must be unique among all live sockets, TIME-WAIT included, and must avoid listened ports: smoltcp doesn't check, and a duplicate tuple mixes users' segments.
> P2-9 A socket in TIME-WAIT, FIN-WAIT or a zero-window persist must stay charged until smoltcp actually frees it, and its linger must be bounded (set_timeout or keepalive). Otherwise close/disconnect churn holds uncharged 16 KiB sockets.
> P2-10 Sizing. in_flight 5 per bucket can't fit sshd (K parked listener ctl reads plus a data read and a Write::Wait per session). The steward's state 16 caps the box's concurrent /net grants. Size these, or state them (the CONTAINMENT sizing rule).
> P2-11 A lying device can boot-loop the box through ipd. smoltcp panics on a non-unicast MAC or address (interface/mod.rs:892, 899). netd must refuse a multicast or zero MAC at bring-up, and args must refuse a non-unicast addr=. ipd must not exit when netd answers `failed` (that means restarts, then init's reboot rule); it should stay up and answer `unreachable`.
> P2-12 The rig is a launcher, so it follows the WP-R3 placement rule (08848f60a): startup page and stack outside 0x1_0000..0x1FF0_0000, with a guard page.
> P2-13 The claim that the pre-K5 happy path needs no timers is wrong for smoltcp as configured: ack_delay defaults to 10 ms (tcp.rs:300). Use set_ack_delay(None), or verify.
> 
> == P3 ==
> - Supply chain: smoltcp's build.rs runs on the host and reads SMOLTCP_* environment variables, which change the compiled config; scrub them or assert none are set. Transitive dependencies are pinned only by Cargo.lock; add a check. Features unify through the host peer Interface's dev-dependency, so give the peer the identical feature set. heapless is used only as Vec and LinearMap, so read those and run Miri over the fuzz corpus.
> - Fuzz statefully (9P, ctl, frames and time together) with the invariants of P1-2b and charge balance, debug assertions on.
> - Grant: require canonical prefixes (host bits zero, len ≥ the held len). The ingress badge can't attach. Restrict new_connection paths to "" and "tcp", or specify socket delegation.
> - On target, give an attacker its scope through typed grant, not only through root arguments.
> - Derive the IRQ from the discovered slot rather than a constant 8 (P2-5's controls make a wrong pairing fail).
> - RST replies to broadcast-addressed SYNs, and 1:1 RST reflection: state them.
> 
> Checked and fine: IPv6 absent (no proto-ipv6); smoltcp drops TCP with an unspecified source or destination (interface/tcp.rs:13-21); the listener is bound to the interface address, so broadcast SYNs don't match; RFC 5961 challenge ACKs present; no ICMP echo or redirects; the ingress badge check; sends max_transfer=1; admission 40 ≤ 48; netd validates the used ring; the kind column and Write::Wait fit the rulings.

> Re-review of plan v2 (the v2 section of the plan file). I checked it against the smoltcp 0.14.0 source, libs/rt (admit.rs AdmitKey::of, the start.rs panic handler) and libslirp/QEMU behaviour.

> 
> == Required in the consolidated plan ==
> R1. The Q147 residual is still understated. The '<= 16 frames, <= 32 KiB at fixed slot offsets' bound is wrong. The RX desc table and avail ring live in the freed RX region too. QEMU virtio-net re-reads avail.idx and the descriptors from guest memory each time a packet arrives (virtio_net_has_buffers, then virtqueue_pop), with no notify needed. So whoever next owns those frames, even an unprivileged process whose map_anon happens to get them, can post descriptors with any physical address, and the next LAN or broadcast frame is DMA'd there: an arbitrary physical write with sender-chosen bytes. The TX side is symmetric: an arbitrary read sent to the wire, if the device flushes or is kicked. Restate it that way. Consequence: the kernel quarantine is a prerequisite for any netd restart (R3) and for use off the bench. D3's bench acceptance can proceed with the residual stated. Notes for the kernel proposal:
> - quarantined frames stay charged (to the dead budget's parent or a kernel reserve) so nothing is overcommitted;
> - reset only devices the loader identified as virtio-mmio (magic and version), since the STATUS offset is virtio-specific;
> - a device that never acknowledges reset keeps its frames for ever (fail safe).
> The panic hook and the other orderly paths are good. Faults such as stack overflow skip the hook and remain the residual.
> 
> R2. The pcap assertion as written fails legitimate traffic, or will be relaxed ad hoc until it proves nothing. hostfwd connections arrive from 10.0.2.2, which is in the self set, so the guest's SYN-ACKs and data in d3-net-tcp (listen) and in any ssh case go to 10.0.2.2. State the rule as:
> - no guest-originated TCP SYN without ACK to a self_forbidden destination;
> - no guest-originated non-TCP IPv4 at all (ipd has none);
> - ARP only for the gateway.
> Classify 'guest-originated' as Ethernet source != slirp's 52:55:0a:00:02:02, which is fail-safe. Fail closed on a truncated, malformed or empty pcap: QEMU may be killed mid-record. Require the positive control's SYN to 10.0.9.100:7 to appear, which proves the capture is live. Derive self_forbidden from the same source as the rig's ipd self= arguments, or check the two are equal. With these, the pcap does prove that no connection attempt toward the self set left the guest NIC: filter-dump sits before slirp, so it sees SYNs that restrict=on later drops.
> 
> R3. The bucket-exhaustion control must prove the cap binds. In the same boot, after K distinct accounts succeed, a (K+1)-th must be refused. Otherwise an ignored buckets= (default 8) passes vacuously. Count every bucket alive at that moment: the rig's own granting badge is account 0 and holds state while its grants live, so it is a bucket too.
> 
> R4. Admission overrides.
> (a) AdmitKey::of uses the raw caller.badge for account 0, so an override applies only to calls on that exact root badge. A connection sshd or the steward mints for itself is a separate default bucket and uses a slot. State that both call on their root badges, or extend the override.
> (b) Apply an override only when caller.account == 0 (ipd can't know a badge's account at parse time). Refuse override badges >= 2^63 and duplicates.
> (c) Startup totals must be sum(overrides) + (buckets - #overrides) x default, both <= 48 and fits.
> The manifest table's 24 + 4x6 = 48 leaves out the steward's own bucket (a sixth), so the arithmetic needs fixing. With (a)-(c), a misconfiguration either fails closed at startup or changes only the misnamed badge's own cap, and isolation between buckets holds.
> 
> R5. Consolidate the file into one clean plan with an OWNER DECISIONS section. The file currently layers v2 dispositions over the v1 body, whose decisions 6 and 11 and parts of sections 1, 3, 5 and 6 are superseded.
> 
> == Verified closed (with small notes) ==
> - P1-1: closed with the cmd: helper. Note: an O_EXCL name of <addr>.<pid> can collide on pid reuse and undercount (the twice twin). Use a unique suffix with a retry, and have the helper refuse to echo if it can't record.
> - /16 layout: the milestone manifest keeps slirp's default /24, which self=10.0.2.0/24 covers fully (vhost .2, DNS .3, every other address). In peer cases the rest of 10.0.0.0/16 maps to host loopback only when restrict is off, and restrict=on is what closes it. Add a qemu.rs unit test asserting that every [net] case emits restrict=on, because the /16 widens the loopback-mapped space.
> - P1-2: the self-unrefused twin catches a missing self check. 'Misordered' overclaims, which is harmless.
> - P1-4: closed. No message carries an address; BROKEN has a random badge and no data; client= is below 2^63. Note: if thread_create fails, reclaim the Box with from_raw and don't retry with it; add the unsafe-budget entry.
> - P1-5: closed.
> - rt panic hook: minimal and acceptable if:
>   - it runs before report_panic, which can block for PANIC_TIMEOUT on the console call;
>   - it has its own once-flag, so a panic inside the hook skips it and exits;
>   - set_panic_hook is set-once;
>   - the hook is bounded and doesn't allocate;
>   - the fn-pointer storage's unsafe is counted in rt's budget.
>   Panic-to-process_exit is unchanged. It goes in the shared-runtime review with Write::Wait, mint_rooted and the Admission override.
> - ISN: verified. Connect and passive open both draw CSPRNG ISNs per connection. poll_ingress_single sends replies (RST, challenge ACK) through the throwaway Interface's empty neighbour cache: they may be lost, as stated, which is acceptable. Add:

>   - info is retried with backoff, so a restarted netd recovers;

### K5b implementer · Question

Event: `0c3146c7c2f2c94d10dc34c6925e6b70` · 2026-09-24T21:04:06Z

> K5b plan v1 (PLAN ONLY). Full text: /home/mick/.claude/plans/wash-inbox-1-message-greedy-whisper.md. Planned against redoubt 816ff9760 + K5 1-4 (ce95d19ba), read-only.
> 
> OWNER DECISIONS (recommendations):
> OD1 Trigger = frames' release, not a last-handle count: before any dma_alloc frame can reach the pool (only when its holder process ends), the kernel resets the device(s) that could hold its address. A handle count can't work: handles copy across tables/messages; a mapping outlives its handle (Q144); init keeps a copy for re-grant, so 'last handle' would never fire on a driver crash. Invariant is at least as strong as 173: nothing is pooled unless its device was reset after it last saw the frame.
> OD2 DMA pages cannot be lent/transferred/process_mapped (InvalidArgument); unmap drops only the PTE, frame stays charged and registered until process end; set_flags works. blkd copies already; D3 netd must not lend DMA memory (confirm).
> OD3 Reset set on death = the device each run was allocated through + every DMA device the process ever map_device'd (a per-process bitmask). Residual: two DMA-trusted processes sharing physical addresses.
> OD4 Poll bound 1000 us on the time CSR + 100000-read backstop, non-preemptible; worst case one bound per device in the set, only for a broken device.
> OD5 Quarantined frames force-charged to the grant holder (device object's owner, system at boot), may exceed its limit (as R3 does); when that budget is destroyed the charge moves to the destroyed top's parent so free pages stay backed by frames. Never re-enter the pool.

### K5 red team · Question

Event: `04b6db60e985acefbe9addd2bf4da1ea` · 2026-09-24T21:07:29Z

> K5b plan v1 red-team review (answer 173, Q147, D3-plan-review R1). Read against the orchestrator's OD1-OD7 rulings, KERNEL-SPEC R3/R10/I5, and the kernel at wp-k5 ce95d19ba: legacy MapMemory, map_range, ownership paths, grants.rs.
> 
> VERDICT: BLOCK on P1-1 (one rule to make explicit, plus a test). Otherwise sound: OD1 (release-time trigger) and the DMA_OWNER sentinel are the right design, and they close the generic free, move and lend paths by construction. P2s to fold into v2.
> 
> Verified by code reading:
> - Only dma_alloc discloses a physical address. The legacy VirtToPhys call is not served (UnhandledSyscall), and legacy MapMemory refuses any range that touches RAM (syscall.rs ~880).
> - Every generic release, move and lend path checks the caller's ownership (release_page, claim_release_move, free_frame_of, move_frame). With the frames owned by DMA_OWNER, none of them can free a DMA frame, including legacy Move/Lend messages and legacy UnmapMemory.
> - process_map moves only is_main_memory pages of the caller's own, so MMIO can't be passed down.
> - A process_create rollback child never ran, so it holds no runs.
> - dma_release inside terminate is non-preemptible, and reset-then-pool happens in one critical section, so no device can be re-armed in between.
> - The window is safe from user space: U bit clear, legacy MapMemory is refused at or above USER_AREA_END for pid != 1, and map_fixed is limited to user space.
> 
> P1-1 A device that is already quarantined must count as NOT reset for every later release.
> s2 step 2 says 'reset every slot in S that is not already quarantined', and step 3 pools runs 'if every reset in S confirmed'. Under the natural reading, a skipped quarantined slot passes step 3.
> Scenario: P1 and P2 both hold runs allocated through device A. P1 dies; A fails its reset, so P1's runs are quarantined and A is flagged. P2 lives on, and A, never successfully reset, still holds ring addresses. P2 dies: A is in S but skipped. If that counts as confirmed, P2's runs go to the pool, which is exactly Q147's arbitrary-DMA hazard.
> The epoch assert doesn't catch it: any successful reset of A after P2's alloc (say a third holder's death, before A broke) satisfies reset_epoch > run.epoch.
> Fix:
> (a) State the rule: a quarantined slot in S means every run of the dying pid is quarantined. Alternatively, quarantine every live run on A at flag time, pooling none later.
> (b) Make the assert specific to this release: record the epoch each slot reached in this dma_release and require it for every run's slot.
> (c) Add a model mutation (e.g. K5bQuarantinedSlotCountsAsReset) and a boot sub-case in dma-reset-quarantine: a second holder on the deaf device dies after the first, and its frames never return.
> 
> P2-1 Legacy MMIO mappings bypass both the reset set and the quarantine flag.
> A grant-holding legacy process can MapMemory a virtio device's MMIO (grants::may_map_device) with no handle. Two consequences:
> (1) It can allocate through device A's handle and drive device B through its legacy mapping. B is not in S, so B keeps the freed frames' addresses.
> (2) A quarantined device stays reachable this way.
> interrupt_claim already refuses IRQs that have a device object ('a source with a device object is R5's'). Do the same for MMIO: refuse legacy MapMemory of any range owned by a device object or registry slot. Otherwise add legacy-mapped registry devices to the process's S bitmask and flag check. Test it in dma-rules.
> 
> P2-2 OD5's over-limit force-charge breaks I5 (usage <= limit). The R3 it cites doesn't allow over-limit: a lend is charged when the receiver takes it, within that receiver's limit.
> A simpler rule keeps I5: quarantine keeps the charge where it already is (the run's charged budget, already paid within its limit). destroy_marked moves it to the destroyed top's parent before return_carve. That parent then gets back the child's carve (>= its usage >= the quarantined pages), so it never goes over its limit, and free pages stay backed by frames. It also removes the recorded grant-holder field and the charge_over function.
> If OD5 stays as written, the docs commit must amend I5, and the model's I5 check must allow it.
> 
> P2-3 Runs are never reclaimed during a process's life. unmap keeps the frame and the run, and the table has 32 runs per device, so a driver that allocates and unmaps dynamically gets OutOfMemory for the rest of its life. It is also charged for every page it ever allocated. Confirm with blkd and D3's netd that each allocates a bounded pool at start (in runs and pages). State in the dma_alloc row that DMA memory is held until the process ends.
> 
> P2-4 The attack case must not pass vacuously, and the must-fail run must fail for the stated reason.
> - Require the reuse to be proven (the same physical address, via the test's own dma_alloc). No reuse is an inconclusive FAIL on both sides, not a pass.
> - The pre-K5b run must record observed DMA into the attacker-steered address, not just a failed expect line.
> - dma-reset-quarantine's 'frames never come back' needs a real search: allocate until the pool (or a bounded large count) is exhausted and assert no quarantined phys appears.
> - Add the co-holder sub-case from P1-1.
> 
> P2-5 Non-virtio DMA devices always quarantine. reset() returns false, so every death of a process whose S contains a non-virtio DMA device quarantines all of its runs and flags that device until reboot, even when the device never saw those frames (OD3 puts every map_device'd DMA device in S). Say so as a platform residual (FPGA and other non-virtio DMA get no restart). Consider flagging only devices that actually held runs, or that were mapped while the process held runs.
> 
> P3:
> 1. Clear the OD3 mapped-device bitmask and every run's holder at terminate. dma_release must consider only Live runs, so that a reused PID never re-processes old Quarantined runs.
> 2. Quarantine doesn't unmap the flagged device from live co-holders (Q144: mappings outlive handles). State it as the residual beside OD3's.
> 3. Billing: under K5's approved rule (s7), destroy work is billed to the dying budget and syscall work to the caller. Bill the reset poll the same way, not 'whichever budget is current'.
> 4. Fix the rv64 window address in the plan and add a boot assert against PLIC, physmap and other kernel windows (rv32 already has one). Confirm the root entry is shared into every process's root.
> 5. The boot classification read of magic and version is harmless for virtio, but other DMA devices in Devs can have read-to-clear registers. Restrict the read to devices the platform marks virtio-mmio, or state it.
> 6. The worst case for K5's latency table: |S| x 1 ms, non-preemptible, on top of R10's ~21 ms. Add it to the sched-latency notes.

> P1-1 CLOSED.
> - reset() returns false without touching a quarantined or non-virtio slot, so such a slot is never in confirmed_now.
> - Step 3 pools only when S is a subset of confirmed_now, and both asserts are per-release. The weak epoch comparison is gone.

> - K5bQuarantinedSlotCountsAsReset and the model's FirstFails device plus the co-holder generator mirror it.
> 
> P2-1 CLOSED as ruled (DMA slots only; the log-server's UART grant at 0x10000000 overlaps no virtio slot, which start at 0x10001000). P3-a below covers the overlap arithmetic.
> P2-2 CLOSED in intent (the charge stays on run.charged; I5 holds), but see N1 on ordering.
> P2-3 CLOSED: the ABI row, blkd 1 run (kernel.rs:67, allocated once), netd 2 runs before thread_create.
> P2-4 CLOSED: reuse proven by phys through dma_alloc, with inconclusive FAIL forbidden; the must-fail run requires observed steered DMA; exhaustive search (but see P3-c).
> P2-5 CLOSED as a stated platform residual, and the reason not to narrow it (a mapped device can hold any of the process's frame addresses) is right.
> P3s CLOSED:
> - the rv64 window at 0xffff_ffff_f400_0000 = KERNEL_PLIC_BASE (0xffff_ffff_f000_0000) + 64 MiB, under the shared root 511, clear of the stacks (fff8_0000) and the image;
> - rv32 at 0xff7f_0000, below PROCESS_AREA 0xff80_0000, with the PLIC-end assert;
> - the boot read limited to loader DMA-flagged (virtio-compatible) entries, with the residual;
> - billing per K5's rule; Live-only runs and state cleared at terminate; the co-holder mapping residual.
> Consistency: OD1-OD7, s2 and the tests agree, with no superseded text.
> 
> N1 (P2) Migrate quarantine charges after return_carve, not before.
> s3 says 'before return_carve(top), every quarantined run charged to a dying budget is re-charged to top's parent, with a plain charge that cannot fail (argued in OD5 and asserted)'. OD5's argument, however, rests on the parent getting back the child's whole carve, which happens in return_carve. Before it, the parent's usage still includes the child's carve, so a limit-checked charge (budget.rs charge() returns Result and boot code .expect()s it) can fail for a parent near its limit, and the assert would panic the kernel (I14).
> Fix: run return_carve(top) first, then charge the parent (q <= top's limit <= the carve just returned, as argued), or apply both as one net adjustment. Keep the assert. Mirror the same order in the model's destroy_budget, and let I5 be checked after each step.
> 
> P3:
> (a) Define 'overlaps a DMA registry slot' by page-rounded ranges. Refuse if [floor(phys), ceil(phys + size)) intersects [floor(base), ceil(base + len)) of any slot, using the Devs entry's length, not only the base. On platforms that pack several device windows into one page, a non-DMA grant on a page shared with a DMA device must be refused too (or the loader must reject such a grant). Test a partial-page and an adjacent-page mapping in dma-rules.
> (b) DMA devices beyond MAX_DMA_DEVICES lose the flag but stay physically DMA-capable. After that they are not in any S, and legacy MapMemory isn't refused for them. Fail closed harder: create no device object for them (the kernel can't police them), and include them in the legacy refusal. Irrelevant on QEMU virt (8 slots); relevant for ports.
> (c) The exhaustive search allocates only against system and one child of users. Any other budget with free pages (the test's own leftover budgets, D1/D2's parents after migration) leaves pool frames the checker never draws, and a wrongly pooled quarantined frame could sit among them. Either destroy every other non-boot budget before searching, or allocate against every budget that still has free pages, and assert the checker's total equals the free-frame count, e.g. from budget_usage(root).
