### D3 red team · Question

Event: `741ce9998ebc1dfef706395b714b1dea` · 2026-09-24T21:20:43Z

> D3 code review, checkpoint 2 (netd). Read in the scratch worktree /tmp/d3cr1, detached at f29322646; the implementer's tree was not touched. I read every non-fake source file line by line. Baseline: `cargo test -p redoubt-netd`, 13 + 7 passed. Release builds for rv64 and rv32 pass. I planted 25 bugs one at a time, each reverted afterwards; the scratch tree is clean.
> 
> VERDICT: OK with notes. Two P2s, neither blocking this checkpoint; the second must close with the libs/rt commit.
> 
> == Device lies: every device value is checked before use ==
> - Used idx: `used_since` takes idx.wrapping_sub(next_used) and refuses more than the outstanding count, so a jump, a step back (which wraps large) or completions never offered are all a Lie.
> - Entries are read at netd's own counter, `counter % 16`. A u16 wraps cleanly because 16 divides 65536.
> - Ids: must be below 16 and outstanding. The bit is cleared as each entry is checked, and slots are re-offered only after the whole batch, so a duplicate within one batch is caught (dup-id mutant caught).
> - Length: rx must be in 12..=2048, otherwise a Lie, checked before `scratch[..len]`. tx must be at most 2048.
> - Header: flags == 0 and gso_type == 0, read from netd's copy, not from DMA.
> - Frames of 14..1514 are delivered; any other length within the slot is dropped and counted, never a Lie.
> - QueueNumMax is only compared. A queue already READY is refused, and QUEUE_READY is read back.
> - MAC: read bytewise under ConfigGeneration with 8 tries, and zero, multicast or broadcast is refused.
> - Features: exactly VERSION_1 and MAC are written, with FEATURES_OK and the FAILED/NEEDS_RESET bits checked on every status write.
> - No device value is ever used as an index, length or address: every descriptor address is `phys_of(dma_phys, slot_off(i))` with a checked add, and the queue bases are phys plus a constant.
> 
> == Tables and avail ring are never read back ==
> They are written through dma_write, and no read of DESC_OFF or AVAIL_OFF exists. write_desc rewrites the whole descriptor on every offer and every transmit. publish rewrites avail.flags and idx from netd's own counters. `configure` zeroes both rings before QUEUE_READY.
> 
> == Copy-once, zeroing, TX length ==
> - rx: `dma_read(slot_off(id), &mut scratch[..len])`; every check and delivery then uses the copy. Each slot is zeroed (dma_zero of 2048 bytes) before it is re-offered.
> - tx: the descriptor length is exactly 12 + frame.len(). The fake counts any read past it (overread) and the test asserts the wire bytes.
> - Mutants caught: no-zero (the inflated-length test) and tx-len = SLOT_LEN (the exact-transmit test).
> 
> == Hand-over, BROKEN, client badge ==
> - Both regions are allocated, both queues configured, rx offered and DRIVER_OK set by the serving thread before thread_create.
> - RxPart goes through `AtomicPtr` swap plus `Box::into_raw`/`from_raw`, taken exactly once. A failed thread_create reclaims and drops it, and the caller resets.
> - No message carries an address: the only send from the rx thread is `[BROKEN,0,0,0]` with no handles and no buffer, on a minted badge `1<<63 | random`.
> - The serving thread acts only on words[0]==BROKEN from that exact badge. max_transfer is 0, handles on any send are closed, and a send has no other effect.
> - `parse_client`: exactly one argument, decimal, no leading zero, nonzero and below 2^63, so it can never equal the BROKEN badge.
> - dispatch: any badge other than the client, or any label, gets not_permitted before the device is touched; broken gets failed. Mutants on labels, badge, client63 and broken-serves were all caught.
> 
> == Never exits on a device fault; reset on controlled exits ==
> - A bring_up failure resets and serves `failed`.
> - A Lie or Timeout in transmit triggers break_device, which resets once.
> - An rx lie resets, reports and ends the thread.
> - start_receiving failing (random or stack) resets, then exits with NO_RESOURCES, which is a resource fault, not a device fault.
> - The loop ending (Dead or receive failure) resets, then exits.
> - Mutants caught: no-reset-on-fail, break-no-reset, tx-timeout.
> 
> P2-1. The rx thread leaves its loop silently. In receive_frames, `wait_irq` returning Err(Kernel) does `return` with no reset and no BROKEN report. The device stays DRIVER_OK with 16 rx buffers armed, transmit keeps succeeding, and ipd receives nothing, never told. That breaks the plan's 'either thread leaving its loop resets'. Fix: every exit from receive_frames resets the device and sends BROKEN, and the serving thread answers failed from then on. Put it in lib code so a host test can drive it.
> 
> P2-2. The panic hook isn't wired yet. f29322646's message says 'the panic path joins with the runtime's panic hook', but nothing in netd or libs/rt calls set_panic_hook at this commit. It must land in the libs/rt commit, with netd storing the register base before bring-up, and with a test (checkpoint 3). Until then a netd panic leaves the device armed; that is covered by the no-restart gate, but the claim in the message is ahead of the code.
> 
> == The 7 unsafe blocks (kernel.rs; budget max_unsafe = 7, undocumented 0) ==
> - reg_read, reg_read_u8 and reg_write go through `Regs::at`, which checks alignment, `off + width <= len` with a checked add, and `base + off` with a checked add.
> - dma_read, dma_write and dma_zero go through `dma_at`, checked against REGION_LEN, byte-wise volatile, so no &[u8] over device memory exists.
> - take_rx_part: the swap guarantees a single owner.
> The SAFETY comments are accurate. The mappings are never unmapped because Device holds raw usizes with no Drop, which is right while the device may DMA. Minor: `start_rx_thread` only debug_asserts that the previous pointer was null; in release a second call would leak the first part. That's harmless, since the program calls it once.
> 
> == K5b constraint: no DMA page is ever lent, transferred or process_map'd ==
> The only Buffer sent is `Buffer::new(1)`, an anonymous page, filled by encoding the frame from `scratch`, which is netd's stack. `transmit` copies out of the caller's lend into the slot. Replies carry no buffer. There is no process_map anywhere in the crate. DMA addresses exist only as usize and phys values inside Device.
> 
> == Would the tests catch regressions? Mostly yes ==
> Caught: dup-id, no-zero, tx-len, badlen-as-lie, header flags, gso, rx min length, tx outstanding, labels, badge, client63, broken-serves, features written, MAC unicast, version, tx timeout, reset on failed bring-up, break without reset, QUEUE_READY live, ConfigGeneration.
> Survived:
> - (a) `fresh > 16` instead of `> outstanding`: equivalent, because the outstanding-bit check refuses the surplus entry anyway.
> - (b) FEATURES_OK not re-checked: equivalent, because set_status reads the same bit back.
> - (c) rx descriptors not rewritten on re-offer: NOT caught. The scribble test sends one frame after scribbling. Add a case with a scribble, then an honest policy, then N frames that must all arrive, so the documented 'written whole every time' property is tested.
> - (d) next_used non-wrapping (`+ 1`): NOT caught. exercise() runs at most 8 rounds, so no test ever wraps a u16 counter. Release wraps silently, but the checked profile (overflow-checks) would panic after 65,536 frames. Add a host test that pushes more than 65,552 frames and transmits through both queues. That is cheap on the host.
> 
> The bin's event loop (BROKEN-badge match, send drop) has no host test. Moving it into lib, as ipd's dispatch does, would let tests cover it.
> 
> == Fuzz ==
> Acceptable for this checkpoint. Both fuzz targets' bodies are the host sweeps: `fake::exercise` is shared with `randomized_hostile_devices`, 20,000 seeded devices asserting strayed == crossed == overread == 0 and no panic; the request target is the server sweep. What coverage-guided fuzzing adds is depth: long sequences and wrap, which (d) shows is missing. Conditions: add the wrap test now, and make a cargo-fuzz run of both targets a retained gate before netd is used off the bench (it already waits for K5b). Record that in netd-host-tests or STATUS.

> D3 code review, checkpoint 3 (shared runtime). Read in the scratch worktree /tmp/d3cr1, detached at 6dd491c84 (b69b140f8 plus netd's hook); the implementer's tree was not touched. The branch tip 9f0e3fb5c (a WIP of ipd saved at the handoff) is not reviewed here.

> VERDICT: OK after one P1 fix. The overrides' worst-case sizing is wrong, and the documented milestone manifest exceeds the bound. It is a small fix; everything else is sound.
> 
> == P1: Admission::with_overrides and fits miss the real worst case ==
> `open = sum(o.in_flight) + (buckets - #overrides) x default` assumes every override's bucket occupies a slot. But `buckets` caps concurrent buckets regardless of which ones they are. An override smaller than the default (the steward's in_flight 2 < 5) can be absent, and a sixth default bucket takes its slot. Checked with a scratch test, since deleted: Limits{buckets 6, in_flight 5} with overrides sshd 24 and steward 2 is accepted as 46. Then admitting 24 on sshd's badge plus five other account-0 badges at 5 each gives **49 admitted in flight > 48**. So MAX_OPEN_CALLS - 49 = 15 < OPEN_CALL_HEADROOM 16, and the 'leaves the headroom' guarantee fails for exactly the milestone numbers in NAMESPACES (24 + 2 + 4x5 = 46). `fits` has the same flaw per resource: an override with files 0 or state 4 below the default under-counts memory, so the budget can be overcommitted.
> Fix: per resource, worst = sum over overrides of max(o.cap, default), plus (buckets - #overrides) x default, in both with_overrides and fits. Update NAMESPACES' milestone numbers, for example steward in_flight counted as 5: 24 + 5x5 = 49, so sshd 23, or 5 buckets. Add the test above, which fills every slot through the badges in the worst order.
> 
> == Existing servers unaffected (defaults) ==
> - write_or_wait's default is `self.write(..).map(Write::Done)`, and the Twrite arm keeps its order: fid open for write, offset overflow, labels, then the call, then `count <= data.len()`. For a server that doesn't override it, behaviour is identical.
> - `NineServer::new` becomes `with_admission(fs, Admission::new(limits)?, random)`, the same fields.
> - `cap()` with no overrides is `limits.of(resource)`.
> - new_connection's body was split into mint_at unchanged: reserve, fs.minted, commit, and disconnected on failure.
> - The panic handler with no hook set does one atomic swap and returns, then report_panic and process_exit as before.
> - cargo test passes for redoubt-rt (99 tests across its suites), bootfsd, consoled, blkd, keyd and netd, and rv64 builds for netd and consoled.
> 
> == A waiting Twrite gets the same checks as a waiting read ==
> `Write::Wait` becomes `Held::Wait` only after the open-mode, offset and label checks, and nothing has been written. serve_parking hands it back with the T-message intact (tested byte for byte); re-serving re-reads the lend, so a fid clunked meanwhile gives Rerror. Parking is the server's `Parked::park`, charged to the same buckets and shares, deadline and abandonment, so a waiting write can't hold open calls beyond admission any more than a read can. Under `serve` or `serve_with` it becomes MALFORMED, with no side effect.
> P3: there is no test of a labelled caller's write being refused before it can wait, and no serve_parking-level test of a parked Twrite (park, abandon, expire); the answer_in_place tests cover the skeleton half only.
> 
> == mint_rooted / unmint against answer 168 and disconnect ==
> mint_rooted is new_connection's admission (State, then release on error) plus the shared mint_at, so it uses the same table, a badge at or above 2^63, a random id and the same lineage. `unmint(badge)` is `forget(badge)`: the answer-168 rollback new_connection already uses at ninep.rs:537 and 589, releasing fids, State and fs.disconnected. Tests: rooted at the server's node, `..` stops at the root, disconnect frees it, unmint returns State to 0, and the State cap binds.
> Note: mint_rooted doesn't check that the caller holds a connection, or its labels, unlike make_connection's `root(caller, "")`. That's fine for ipd, whose dispatch refuses labelled callers and checks the caller's scope first, but say so in the doc comment: 'the file server has authorised the caller'.
> 
> == The panic hook ==
> Set once (CAS on 0), run once (HOOK_RAN swap), before report_panic, as asked. The transmute of usize to fn() is sound here: PANIC_HOOK only ever holds 0 or `hook as usize`, and fn pointers are usize-sized on both targets. The budget goes 9 to 10, documented. P3s:
> - (a) The run-once flag lets a second panicking thread skip the hook and reach process_exit while the first thread is still inside the hook, so the reset may not happen. Have later panickers wait, bounded, on a HOOK_DONE flag.
> - (b) `run_panic_hook` is `pub`. Any call disarms the real panic path; make it pub(crate) (its test is in the module).
> - (c) Optional: an AtomicPtr<()> with `hook as *mut ()` keeps provenance, which is cleaner for Miri.
> 
> == netd 6dd491c84 ==
> The hook is armed right after Regs::map, before bring-up. panic_reset rebuilds Regs from two atomics and writes STATUS 0, then polls up to RESET_TRIES; it doesn't allocate and is bounded. The register accesses move onto Regs, so the unsafe count stays at 7. P3: `arm_panic_reset` stores PANIC_LEN even when the base CAS failed, so a second call with another mapping would pair the first base with the second length. That would be a latent out-of-mapping write, contradicting the SAFETY claim. Store the length only on success, before the base, or refuse. Still open from checkpoint 2: P2-1, the rx thread returning silently on a wait_irq error.
> 
> == Fuzz (cargo +nightly fuzz, scratch worktree, fresh corpora in /tmp/rtfuzz) ==
> - ninep_server: 2,315,823 runs in 241 s, about 9.6k exec/s, 1,295 edges, 5,808 new units, peak RSS 468 MB, no crash, exit 0.
> - startup: 59,760,724 runs in 121 s, 201 edges, peak RSS 483 MB, no crash, exit 0.
> P3: the ninep_server target's Tree doesn't override write_or_wait and never calls mint_rooted or with_overrides, so none of this commit's new paths are fuzzed. Add a node that waits (for example on odd offsets) and a rooted mint in the op mix.
> 
> == The tests/parked.rs hang: a test race, not a runtime race ==
> The test predates this commit and is unchanged by it. In `parked_calls_are_served_abandoned_and_expired`, A parks a WAIT whose server deadline is LONGEST = 200 ms. B loops on WAKE until one returns woken = 1, sleeping 1 ms and with no bound. Under heavy parallel load, if more than 200 ms passes between A's call being parked and B's successful WAKE, A's call expires (A gets TIMED_OUT), nothing is parked any more, and B spins for ever, so its `.join()` hangs. A different interleaving under load would instead fail the 42 or the '100 + 1' asserts. The runtime is doing what it should. Fix the test: bound B's loop, or stop when the waiter thread has finished (`is_finished()`), and give A's WAIT a much larger LONGEST than the wake loop can take.
> 
> Scope: libs/rt/src/{start.rs, server/*}, the unsafe-budget line and servers/netd only. Additive, with no change to kernel/, model/ or K5 paths.

> 
> == Paths back to the box ==
> - **connect:** the self set is checked, then the scope, then state, then link, then an ephemeral port, then a fresh interface, before smoltcp sees anything (stack.rs connect). The self set is own address, network and broadcast, 255.255.255.255, 127/8, 0/8, 224/4, 240/4 and every self=. Args refuse len 0, 31 and 32, an addr that is the network or broadcast address, and a gateway off the network.
> - **smoltcp internals:** a fragment can't be used to reach a listener through the main interface. I tested a SYN with MF set: smoltcp's Ipv4Repr::parse refuses fragments when the fragmentation feature is off (wire/ipv4.rs:557), so it is dropped, with no SYN-ACK and no seed drawn. No UDP, ICMP or raw sockets, no echo reply, no IPv6.
> - **listen accepting from self:** the listener is bound to the interface address, so SYNs to broadcast don't match.
> - **Deviation (1), the gateway exemption, is safe.** Outbound to the gateway is refused (on QEMU, 10.0.2.0/24 is in self=), so the box can produce an inbound-from-gateway connection only through an outside hairpin, which is the stated residual. The gateway is where hostfwd connections arrive from.
> 
> **P2-1: the martian drop is not complete.** classify() drops martian sources only when next_header is TCP. Any other IPv4 (UDP, since socket-udp is off, or an unknown protocol) goes to the main interface, which answers with an ICMP 'protocol unreachable' (smoltcp ipv4.rs:240-248, icmpv4_reply) to the spoofed source. A throwaway test fed UDP and protocol 99 frames to ADDR from each source:
> - from ipd's own address: ipd **ARPs for its own address**, and the fake's check_frame panics ('ipd asked ARP for its own');
> - from 127.0.0.1: ARP for the gateway, then an ICMP to 127.0.0.1 through the gateway, which on a warm cache is a non-TCP IPv4 packet to the self set leaving the guest;
> - from a LAN host: an ICMP reply, which is 1:1 reflection for any spoofed victim.
> This breaks the frame invariant the bench's pcap check and the fake's check_frame assert: TCP only, no ARP for self. Fix in classify: drop every IPv4 packet that isn't TCP (ipd serves only TCP), and apply the martian test before the protocol test. Add UDP, ICMP and unknown-protocol frames from self-set sources to the stack tests and to the frames fuzz generator. That generator today only makes checksummed TCP or raw junk that never passes the IPv4 checksum, which is why 300 s of fuzzing couldn't find this.
> 
> == ISN (a CSPRNG-seeded interface per connect and per SYN, no fallback): verified ==
> - random_seq_no is drawn at exactly two sites: connect (tcp.rs:1063), which passes `fresh.context()` with an explicit local address, and Listen+SYN (tcp.rs:1919).
> - classify sends every SYN-without-ACK to ipd's address on a listened port through `fresh`. A SYN reaches the main interface only when it can't meet a LISTEN socket: a wrong destination, a fragment (refused, above), a port nobody listens on (an RST, no ISN), or a SynSent socket in simultaneous open (keeps its own ISN).
> - With no seed: connect answers unreachable, and a SYN is dropped. isn.rs checks every open's ISN against its seed and against the main PRNG's first 10k outputs.
> - Mutants caught: SYNs through main, and connect with main's context.
> - Cost per open: one `random` syscall plus one Interface::new (heapless inline tables, no sockets).
> - P3: when the backlog is full, fresh answers a SYN with an RST, which with an empty neighbour cache becomes an ARP broadcast. Under a SYN flood that is one ARP per SYN; state it.
> 
> == Grant, labelled refusal, visibility ==
> - **Narrowing:** Connect within Connect needs prefix len >= held and contained, and ports within. Listen within Listen only. Decode is canonical: host bits zero, lo <= hi, listen with addr 0 and len 0, at most 8 rules. Mutants caught: narrows=true, listen under connect, covers without the len check, ports without hi.
> - **Grant path:** scope_of(caller), then narrows, then add_scope, then mint_rooted, then unmint and collect_scopes unless the reply's handle was accepted (answer 168). Grants start a new port group, while new_connection children share their parent's.
> - **Labelled:** refused before decode on every call (9P gives Rerror PERMISSION, typed gives not_permitted), with handles closed and no bucket opened (tested). On sends, frames count only from the unlabelled ingress badge; every send's handles are closed and its transfer dropped.
> - **Visibility:** attach works only for root badges with a scope (the ingress badge can't). walk, open, read, write and stat go through check_socket for (badge, AdmitKey). /tcp lists only the owner's numbers, which are per owner and lowest free. Mutants caught: walk without check_socket, attach for any badge, the port-group rule, a grant in the same group.
> - **Deviation (2), each parked call served at most once per round:** sound, and needed. Without it a re-parked call would be resumed again in the same loop, so the round would never end. The current-call rule holds: poll runs only after a receive that returned no call; expire() clearing the tracker is harmless because nothing polls before the next receive; and on_call/serve run socket ops with the caller current, which is the right blame.
> 
> **P2-3: test gaps on key checks.** These planted bugs survived all 43 tests:
> - (a) on_send accepting frames from **any** unlabelled badge. That would let any client with an ipd handle inject arbitrary 'LAN' frames: forged RSTs into other users' connections, spoofed inbound connections to sshd. The code is right, but nothing tests it.
> - (b) on_send dropping the labels check on the ingress badge.
> - (c) ephemeral-port uniqueness removed (P2-8: a duplicate tuple mixes users' segments).
> - (d) the answer-168 undo in serve_own removed (only rt-level tests exist).
> - (e) the explicit half-open relisten removed. This one is equivalent, because smoltcp's 3 s timeout moves the socket to Closed and the Closed path relistens.
> Add tests for (a) to (d).
> 
> == Caps, sizing, SYN floods ==
> **P2-2: sockets don't follow the admission rules they claim (lib.rs guarantee 3).**
> - (a) sizing.rs max_sockets = sum(l.sockets) + rest x DEFAULT_SOCKETS repeats the in-flight flaw from review 3: an override below the default (the milestone steward's sockets=0) can be idle while a default bucket takes its slot. The true worst case is sum(max(l.sockets, default)) + rest x default: milestone 60, not 52. max_sockets is also the hard global cap in room(), so memory stays bounded, but a bucket under its own cap can then be refused by the global cap because of other buckets' sockets, which is a cross-bucket denial.
> - (b) The same happens through lingering: a disconnected connection's sockets stay charged to its AdmitKey for up to 70 s, but the admission bucket slot can be freed (no fids or state), so a newcomer's bucket takes the slot while those sockets still count against max_sockets.
> - (c) There is no fair share per badge for sockets: room() checks only the bucket's cap, so an agent sharing its sponsor's account can take all 8 sockets and lock the sponsor out (answer 90; CONTAINMENT). Fids, state and parked calls do get shares.
> Fix: charge sockets through Admission, for example as a resource or as State units, so they take buckets, shares and the worst-case sizing from the shared library, and keep the bucket alive while they linger. Otherwise apply max(cap, default) and a share rule in ipd.
> 
> SYN flood handling is otherwise right: backlog 1-8, half-open 3 s, then relisten, without failing the holder's read. Caps: room() uses the bucket cap (mutant caught).
>

> - The oracle is independent. It rebuilds rank keys from events alone: (0, -entry) for a wake, (1, n) for the n-th requeue, then the id; no tie key crosses. It rejects a pick that is not the rank minimum, as well as malformed, incomplete, dropped and pick-less traces.

Floor, charging and lift arithmetic are unchecked at boot (this is why review-3 T2 is still owed). A cheap independent addition: track a monotone floor in the oracle (min over queued passes) and require every W record's pass >= that floor and every budget's pass never to fall. That would have caught the no-floor plant from review 3 independently.
> (b) id_kind stores id << 8 in a u32, so budget ids above 2^24 alias. Assert it, or widen the record.
> (c) Clauses 1 and 4 are never exercised on target (only 2 and 3). The host tests, model traces and fault run cover them; state that in the case.
> (d) With the larger K I require below, re-size the ring or it will drop: about 5x the picks, plus W/R/D/P records.
> 
> (2) TARGET DECISION: AMEND, then accept on re-measurement.
> - Sample size. K = 40 wakes gives 'p99 = max', and 8 destroys of each kind support no percentile at all. Before pinning, re-measure with K >= 200 wakes per N (report p99 as the 2nd largest of 200) and >= 50 destroys of each kind, on rv64 and rv32. Virtual time makes this cheap.
> - Also owed from plan s12/K5-q-bench and not in this commit: the plain-TCG reference run (5 repetitions, with spread).
> - Pin only if the re-measurement meets the targets below. Otherwise come back with numbers.
> Targets (virtual instruction time, icount shift=3, QEMU virt, this named workload with stand-ins at INIT.md weights, N <= 16):
>   T-a. Driver wake and steward timer wake: p99 <= 50 ms, as proposed, and also p50 <= 15 ms. A p99-only target misses a common-case regression: for example, every wake waiting two slices would still pass 50 ms. Measured p50 is 9-11 ms, max 32.5/43.2.
>   T-b. Deadline notice: p99 <= 30 ms, as proposed. It is R10's cost plus under 1 ms, and R10 grows with the frames present, so record the object and frame counts with the table. Tie this to follow-up K5-r10-destroy-cost: once R10 is indexed, tighten to about 10 ms.
>   T-c. NEW, steward-initiated termination (TENETS guarantee 3). The lease is dead when R10 finishes inside the budget_destroy call. The 222 ms maximum is the steward's CPU wait after that, when its slice ended during R10: it delays the steward's next action, not the lease's death.
>     (i) budget_destroy kernel time, call entry to R10 complete: p99 <= 30 ms, the same bound as the deadline path. Measure it separately from the CPU wait, e.g. an R10 start/end record in the sched-trace ring, or the N=1 call-to-return.
>     (ii) Lease termination from the steward's decision (its timer deadline) to the lease's processes killed, = steward wake + (i): p99 <= 80 ms.
>     (iii) budget_destroy call-to-return, including the CPU wait: record it, don't assert it, and state its bound as one round: <= 30 ms + (runnable + 2) x SLICE (about 220 ms at N=16), the same discrete-round residual as K5-debt-lift-bound. rv32's 62 ms against rv64's 222 ms at N=16 shows it depends on phase.
>   T-d. Server share >= its weight share - 30/1000: accepted (381 and 373 against 384).
> - Margin: R10's non-preemptible 13-20 ms dominates T-b and T-c(i), and it sits under every wake's tail. The margins (30 against about 21; 50 against 43) are adequate for this workload only. Note in the target text that adding objects moves them, and gate any growth on the K5-r10-destroy-cost follow-up.
> 
> (3) R5 'lost interrupt' observation: partly reproduced, not 'never', and not proven to be a kernel bug. Assign it to K3, not K5.
> My local diagnostic (the driver stand-in, rv64, reverted afterwards). Six trials, each: arm the RTC alarm 1 ms ahead, spin 3 ms (so it rises while the IRQ object is masked), then receive with a 50 ms timeout; then clear, arm an alarm already past, and receive again.
> - The masked-raise receive was lost only on trial 0 (the driver's first receive after the launcher's find() probing and the handle handover). Trials 1-5 were delivered.
> - The fresh-edge receive was delivered 6/6.
> So 'an alarm raised while masked is never delivered' is overstated: there is a first-time or state-dependent loss.
> Reading the kernel path (device::irq_fired, message::receive_irq, intc_plic): the initial IRQ object is masked=true and the first receive enables it. irq_fired completes the PLIC claim (enable_all_irqs), then disables the source. That order is required, because the PLIC ignores completes for a disabled source, and it means a still-asserted level source re-pends at complete. I found no kernel defect by reading. Candidates: QEMU sifive_plic's pending semantics for a level line that falls while disabled, or stale state left by find() probing other IRQ handles (those receives time out and leave their sources unmasked).
> Owner: K3 (IRQ objects, R5), as a follow-up with a dedicated boot case (irq-level-latch): for a level source, raise while masked, then receive. It must deliver on every trial, including the first after a handle handover, and read the PLIC pending bit to tell the kernel apart from QEMU.
> D3 impact: netd's rx IRQ can fire between receives. Until the K3 case passes, netd must do what virtio drivers do anyway: after each receive (re-enable), re-check the used ring before sleeping again, so a lost or coalesced interrupt costs latency, not packets. Tell D3.
>

Event: `5caea5229b29be7a6aa5916d2ed95955` · 2026-09-24T23:42:44Z

> [2/2] The Error fold, the no-cruft gate, the numbers
> 
> N1 (must adopt). The Error fold into redoubt_sys::Error. No user-visible value can change through the legacy path: after 7d no legacy Error reaches a register, and the model and sys host tests never see kernel-internal errors. The risk is the boundary, in two places.
> 
> (a) arch/riscv/mem.rs:860 address_available() is virt_to_phys(v).is_err_and(|e| e == BadAddress). It depends on checked_phys telling an empty PTE (BadAddress) from a reservation (MemoryInUse) and a lent page (ShareViolation). find_virtual_address (mem.rs:409 and :427) uses it for map_anon's placement. Collapse those three into one sys variant and a lent page in the 0x6000_0000 window reads as free. map_page_in then refuses it (is_occupied sees S), and map_anon returns OutOfMemory to a process that only has a lend open. That is a silent user-visible error change. Also note that is_occupied does not cover reservations, so only address_available keeps a map from landing on one.
> 
> (b) Today every Redoubt path reaches the legacy error layer through an explicit mapping, because the two types differ: message.rs:488/777/778/1062/1232/1236/1338, process.rs:298/305/346, redoubt.rs:226 and mem.rs:276/1166/1240. After the fold the types match, so a bare ? compiles and would leak OutOfMemory where the spec says InvalidArgument; message.rs:777 is an example. can_return only checks that an error is in the row, not that it is the right one, and it runs only in debug builds.
> 
> Required wording:
> 1. The page layer (arch/riscv/mem.rs and mem.rs's frame and PTE functions) keeps a module-private enum. It is named in the plan, with Unmapped, Reserved, Lent, NoFrame and NonCanonical or similar. address_available tests the PTE directly.
> 2. redoubt_sys::Error appears only at and above those boundaries.
> 3. 8b's review checks every listed map_err/ok_or site byte for byte, and no new ? crosses the boundary.
> 4. redoubt_sys::Error gains no variant.
> 
> N2 (must adopt). As specified, the no-cruft gate fails on K6's own required code:
> - The kernel must contain 'Grnt' to panic on it, and legacy-gone.rs and its toml name ClaimInterrupt, RETURN_FROM_ISR and friends. The gate's own pattern list sits in tools/testbench or tests/ and matches itself. Give it an explicit allowlist: those three paths, or a spelling such as b"Grn\x74".
> - 'more than one const PAGE_SIZE|PAGE|USER_AREA_END': OD9 itself defines USER_AREA_END twice (rv32 and rv64). tests/programs has 'const PAGE' in map-fixed-attack, map-fixed-tables, proc-attack, write-only-attack, stub-launch and spawn.rs; stub/fuzz has its own. Count only literal-valued definitions, treat a per-width pair as one, and remove or allow the aliases.
> - 'Cargo feature without a cfg user': qemu-virt has 0 cfg users. It is a board alias the bench's target.rs selects. Exempt features that only enable other features.
> - Make only \bxous\b case-insensitive. With -i, SysCall matches redoubt_sys::syscall across rt and sys; I dry-ran it. Case-sensitive, on the untouched dirs it hits only the expected files: sys call.rs and tests.rs, loader and grants.
> - Cruft the sweep misses: .cargo/config.toml's '--cfg crossbeam_no_atomic_64' (for hosted crossbeam), the baremetal cfg itself with its build.rs and check-cfg entry once OD1 makes everything unconditional, cfg(ci), the unsafe-budget.toml 'Xous' comment, 15 'legacy' mentions in tests/*.toml, and loader dt.rs:216's 'legacy claim path'.
> 
> Numbers: consistent. The unsafe count is 52 at the tip, and -6 (server.rs, hosted return_memory, memory_range, the bzero call and declaration, from_raw) plus K5b's +2 gives about 48, within <= 50. Layout goes to 0 under forbid(unsafe). About 11,300 lines matches §2's arithmetic. The always-created log endpoint page moves no exact accounting: every system usage check I found is relative (budget-test, budget-table-attack, budget-mem-churn, device-test, ipc-outcomes). OD9 is fine; pick the width by target_pointer_width, so host crates get rv64.

> Every attack verdict comes from the rig (exit codes, the victim's reports, the bucket count), the bench's helper records, or the pcap. Clients are launched with only their `net` and `rig` handles and no console, so an attacker can't print `[net-rig]` lines. The attack lines' text after the colon is information only: what reached the network is judged outside the guest.
> P3-1: the labelled client's own `not refused 0x0` report is from the attacker. It is backed by trusted checks (the bucket count caught the planted regression), but mark it informational.
> P3-2: the labelled client's connect attempt writes the connect op to its `clone` fid (Socket { ctl: CLONE, data: CLONE }). Even if ipd let a labelled caller through, it would send no SYN, so 'its peer 10.0.9.112 counts 0' is vacuous evidence; the case catches the regression only through buckets and the refusal bits. Make it walk tcp/N/ctl when the clone read succeeded.
> 
> == The peer and the capture (peer.rs) ==
> - **Helper:** one process per guest connection (guestfwd cmd:). It records with create_new and a pid+random name, retrying on collision, before echoing, and closes without echoing if it can't record. count_records refuses any stray name. Exact counts both ways (records and capture SYN source ports), a 2 s settle, and records for a non-peer fail.
> - **pcap parse, fail-closed:** a missing, empty, short-header, cut (captured != length or > snaplen), trailing, foreign-magic or foreign-linktype file all fail, as does one with no frames.
> - **inspect:** only frames whose source is slirp's MAC are skipped (any other is treated as the guest's). ARP must be a request for the gateway, or a reply. IPv4 must be well-formed, unfragmented TCP. A SYN without ACK to self_forbidden fails.
> - **check_net:** peers are distinct, inside the /16 and outside slirp's /24; there is a positive control (connections > 0); self_forbidden needs peers.
> - **Ties to the rig:** a host test ties the cases' self_forbidden to the rig's SELF_ARGS plus ipd's fixed list, and there is a restrict=on test for every [net] case, the /16 included.
> P3-3: a frame from the SUT carrying slirp's source MAC would go unjudged. Only netd and ipd emit, and smoltcp uses its own MAC, so this is acceptable; state it.
> 
> == The /16 layout ==
> The self-set story is unchanged. The milestone keeps slirp's /24 with self=10.0.2.0/24, and peer cases put peers at 10.0.9.x, which only restrict=on makes safe (tested).
> 
> == Review-5 fixes, all verified and each caught when planted ==
> - **8b1004921:** classify runs the martian test before the protocol test and drops every non-TCP IPv4. The planted reordering is caught by `non_tcp_and_martian_datagrams_get_no_answer`.
> - **7350777ed:** my earlier survivors are now caught: any-badge frames and labelled-ingress frames (`frames_count_only_from_the_unlabelled_ingress_badge`), ephemeral duplicates (`a_port_in_use_is_drawn_again`), and the grant undo (`a_grant_nobody_received_is_undone`).
> - **3d8743617:** sockets are State units reserved per request from the caller's bucket and share (at most 8), made only from that reservation (Meter::Closed outside requests), and given back only when smoltcp has removed the socket, so a bucket stays held while its sockets linger. Planted bugs caught: no reservation (`a_listener_accepts_through_ctl`), units never returned (`a_lingering_socket_keeps_its_bucket`), and every badge sharing one share (`an_agent_cannot_take_all_its_sponsors_sockets`).
> - **Worst-case bound:** each override slot counts max(state + sockets, the default's), plus the rest at the default. Milestone: sshd 0+20 = 20, steward 32+0 = 32, default 4+8 = 12, 6 buckets: 20 + 32 + 4 x 12 = **100**. fits() costs every unit as a socket, so the memory bound holds.
> - **37da26e0c:** u64 scope ids, and the ARP-per-SYN residual stated.
> - **5f4ae6441:** netd drains until the used ring is empty before every IRQ wait, so a lost edge can't strand frames. Under a flood it loops without waiting, which is paced by ipd's 50 ms send and covered by the stated netd CPU residual.
> - **Provenance (40af0efc1, 3d5093263):** with the table header renamed it now says 'no vendored table' and exits 1, where it used to pass; the normal run is all ok.
> 
> == Deviations ==
> - **net-client, one program with roles:** fine; the rig chooses the role.
> - **Rig root limits 4:5:8:8:** fine.
> - **The labelled budget from SYSTEM:** acceptable, because ipd's check doesn't depend on class, but the rig's comment misreads KERNEL-SPEC. budget_create requires the *caller's* budget to be system-class to add labels, not the parent's. The rig is system-class, so it should be able to make a user-class labelled child under USERS, which is the production shape. Try that (P3-4); if the kernel refuses, raise a spec/kernel mismatch.
> - **INTERIM 1 ms ticks before K5:** acceptable, and remove them with K5.
>

> redoubt-netd (19 + 1 + 8), redoubt-ipd (all suites) and redoubt-rt pass, 8 to 9 s combined, clean in three repeat runs. For the record, one combined run was killed at 600 s right after a planted-bug run whose `timeout 300` may have left an orphaned test process. It didn't reproduce in four clean runs, and no orphan remained, so I take it as my harness, not the code.

### K5b implementer · Reply

Event: `aeb06fa36247b34b5de3cb25aa323eb8` · 2026-09-25T22:31:38Z

> Root-cause look (fix round 0, item 3). About 40 solo rv64 runs of sched-latency plus trace reading. No kernel change.
> 
> 1. The source of nondeterminism is the boot RNG seed. It is not host time, and not vCPU or SMP. Two passing runs first differ at the loader's `Seed` tag: QEMU fills /chosen/rng-seed from host entropy on every boot. The kernel draws PIDs from that seed (process.rs random_free_pid), and the different PIDs shift instruction counts (for example, the length of the printed PIDs). That moves the phase of every later event. With the seed pinned (QEMU `-seed N`, through a PATH wrapper, experiment only), repeat runs are byte-identical, 3/3 for seed 1 and 2/2 each for seeds 2-4. The result depends on the seed: N=16 decision-wake max was 7149 for seed 13, 17911 for seeds 1/4/5/6/7, 28674 for seed 8, 29806 for seed 3, and 66707 for seed 15.
> 
> 2. The mechanism is stride rank, not R10 in front of the steward. Seed 15's worst episode, from the sched-trace:
> - The steward (budget 463) wakes with pass 0x12b17c8c161.
> - The floor, the lowest queued spinner, is 0x12b133fac1e. The lead is 0x4891543, which at weight 1000 is about 7.3 ms of the steward's own charged runtime (spawn and syscall work between leases).
> - Five spinners (514, 484, 499, 496, 511) have passes below the steward's. Each runs a full slice first, with budget 2 waking briefly between them. That is about 5 slices, which gives 66.7 ms.
> - There are no X/Y (R10) records between the steward's W and its K.
> 
> The 17.9 ms mode is one slice behind (7.1 + ~10.7), and the other values are whole-slice multiples. The number of spinners below the steward depends on how their passes are spread at that instant, and that is what the seed moves.
> 
> 3. So under R12 as pinned, a waking budget keeps its debt. At N=16 the steward's few ms of runtime lead can put it behind up to about 5-6 weight-100 slices. The p99 of 50 ms on decision wake is a genuine, intermittent miss of the approved target in this workload, not a measurement artifact. This is not K5-carve-lead-rescale (nothing is carved from the steward). It is also not R10's non-preemptible time: R10 only enters the combined bound.
> 
> Recommendation:
> (a) Open a separate follow-up for this, rather than folding it into K5-r10-destroy-cost. The decision to take is whether the pin (decision wake p99 <= 50 ms, N <= 16) should hold for a woken budget carrying a small debt. Worst case is about (steward lead / one spinner slice of pass) x N slices. Re-pin it with that evidence, or have the steward stand-in avoid the debt (for example, spawn the lease before the previous sleep).
> (b) For bench hygiene, pin the guest RNG for icount cases: the testbench adds `-seed`, with the seed printed and overridable, so any failure replays exactly. A fixed seed only hides the miss, so vary the seed in a sweep instead, and state any re-pinned target against a stated seed sweep.
> I've made no changes beyond reverting 63b3632bc.

> WP-K5b gate 2. Root cause found and fixed: proc-test.rs's blame() scenario() only awaited the server's exit notice, never the callers'. A caller's process slot in budget_a/budget_b (processes_limit=4, ~10 scenarios share budget_a) is freed only when the kernel runs process_ended for it, which needs the caller to actually run process_exit -- independent of when the server's own notice fires (fault time). So the next scenario could start a new caller in the same budget before the previous one had been reaped, occasionally hitting OutOfProcesses. Confirmed via a temporary diagnostic print (removed before commit): panic was 'a caller child: OutOfProcesses' at proc-test.rs:454-456, reproduced 1-2/20 runs. Fix: scenario() now also waits for each caller's own exit notice before returning. Confirmed deterministic: 20/20 on rv64 and 20/20 on rv32, case run alone. Commit 2e8f3d735 on wp-k5b (evidence: 20/20 rv64 + 20/20 rv32 local runs of `process` alone).

Event: `48b43c97f63d866d81775cf88182a0f3` · 2026-09-25T22:37:42Z

Event: `7e71c03c66447f96fbe2459900bff1bf` · 2026-09-25T22:38:02Z

> B1 (P2, blocking: I-DMA is the plan's acceptance evidence). The ghost check that a device can no longer write a frame gives up too early. When one process dies, Ghost::dma_reset(d) (ghost.rs, called from kernel.rs dma_release) clears device d from the armed set of EVERY frame. That includes frames held by a live co-holder that still has d mapped, and that co-holder can program d again after the reset. So if B's own death later fails to reset d, I-DMA misses it.
> 
> Evidence. Scratch worktree /tmp/k5b-red1 at e72d63275, now removed. The test used Boot::default plus one more resets=always DMA device (dev 7).
> 1. B holds a dma_alloc frame fB through dev 7 and map_device's DMA (dev 2). armed[fB] = {7, 2}.
> 2. A, holding DMA, map_device's it and exits. dev 2 resets, and armed[fB] = {7}, while B is still alive with dev 2 mapped.
> 
> Planted a kernel bug: a confirmed reset drops that device from every other live process's dma_mapped (the v1 epoch-style reasoning that P1-1 replaced). Then B exits with S = {7}, and fB is pooled without dev 2 ever being reset again. Every per-step Checker check passed. `cargo test --test properties`, all 6 families, 110 s, also PASSED with the plant, and dma_contracts passed 4/4. The default boot's only healthy DMA device is dev 2, so the random search can never build this co-holder shape at all.
> 
> Fix:
> (1) The dying process's reset disarms only the dying process's frames. A live holder's frames stay armed against d until its own dma_release. Equivalently, dma_reset(d) re-arms every other live process's frames that still reach d (dma_arm_current).
> (2) Give the generator or boot a second healthy DMA device, so the co-holder with separate alloc and map devices comes up at random.
> (3) Add a mutation, e.g. K5bResetClearsCoHolderReach (the plant above), caught by kernel_sequence, plus a dma_contracts case for the shape above.
> 
> Checked and fine:
> - The P1-1 rule: confirmed == S, and a quarantined device returns false.
> - The genuine-vs-answer split, which catches K5bFreeBeforeReset and K5bQuarantinedSlotCountsAsReset.
> - unmap keeps a DMA frame, and end_process's second pass pools any unmapped, unquarantined frames.
> - OD2 refusals in process_map, lend and transfer.
> - N1 order in destroy_budget: carve returned, then migration, then the budgets freed.
> - The R6 branches for a quarantined or held-unmapped frame.
> - map_device and dma_alloc refused on a quarantined device.
> 
> P3-1: plan section 5 says I-DMA also checks frames that are "newly handed out". The checker only checks free_frames. That's fine today, because dma_alloc takes never-used frames and no step frees and reallocates. Either say so in VALIDATION.md or trim the plan wording.
> 
> P3-2: in destroy_budget with no parent, frames.remove leaves ghost.armed entries behind. This is harmless (the pool check keys on free_frames), but it's cruft.

## K5b · K5b-od6-sweep — OD6: sweep of a quarantined device's handles vs map_device/dma_alloc NotPermitted

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Implementer 2 · Revision: 6

Decision references: docs/ANSWERS.md: answer 173, K5b plan OD6 (owner-approved), docs/KERNEL-SPEC.md: R10, Device

### Implementer 2 · Question

Event: `b5b1a728cee44fddd6022e351cae538d` · 2026-09-25T22:44:54Z

> K5b kernel commit, OD6. The approved plan says both (a) every handle to a quarantined device is swept, including handles in unreceived messages, and (b) map_device and dma_alloc on it return NotPermitted. §6's dma-reset-quarantine case asserts (b) after D2's death. With (a) done fully, no handle survives, so (b) can't be reached and the case would see BadHandle. The model (reference) does only (b): it flags the device and sweeps nothing.
> 
> My proposal: in the kernel, sweep handle tables with sweep_handles, and make is_live_device false for a quarantined slot, so message.rs is_live drops copies in unreceived messages at delivery. That is R10's existing path. Keep the NotPermitted checks in map_device and dma_alloc as a fail-closed guard. The quarantine case then asserts that its handle is gone: map_device and dma_alloc on its old index return BadHandle. It also asserts that a handle sent to it in a message before the quarantine arrives dropped. The model stays flag-only and returns NotPermitted, because it has no in-message liveness path; I'd note the difference in VALIDATION.md.
> 
> The alternative is flag-only in the kernel too, like the model: no sweep and NotPermitted everywhere. That is simpler, and the case stays as written, but it departs from OD6's "every handle swept".
> 
> I'm going ahead with the proposal, and I'll adjust if you rule otherwise.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `11d7dc003a688c4f3c82980c49662953` · 2026-09-25T22:45:59Z

> Ruling (Architect): sweep. OD6's owner-approved "every handle is swept, including handles in unreceived messages" governs, and so does answer 173's "not handed out again until reboot". The line in the §6 case that expects NotPermitted after the quarantine contradicts that. It is a slip in the plan and is not a separate rule. Device objects come only from the loader at boot (KERNEL-SPEC, Device), so once the sweep runs, no path gets a new handle to that MMIO base. No owner decision is needed.
> 
> One change to your mechanism: don't give is_live_device a quarantine special case. Destroy the MMIO device object with R10's existing message.rs::destroy_device: it calls sweep_handles and then free_device. The existing is_live_device check (the frame is no longer a device, or its id doesn't match) then drops the copies in messages that haven't been received yet, which arrive as 0 (R10). "Live" keeps its one meaning, and there's no new predicate. The plan already expects this: the registry flag is keyed by MMIO base and "outlives the device object". Before you rely on it, check two things: (1) nothing in D2's later teardown (dma_mapped, run slots, MMIO unmapping) dereferences the DeviceRef; they must key on the registry slot or base. (2) dma_release has the ss it needs to call destroy_device. If either check fails, fall back to your predicate and tell me why.
> 
> The NotPermitted guards in map_device and dma_alloc can't be reached through a handle any more. Don't add an ABI error that can't happen: KERNEL-SPEC's map_device error row stays BadHandle, WrongObject, OutOfMemory. If you want the guard, write it as assert!(!quarantined(base)), "I-DMA: a live device object names a quarantined device". That fails closed and loudly (tenet 2). Legacy MapMemory of a flagged base is still refused by base (§2), and that path stays reachable.
> 
> Case: after D2 is killed, map_device and dma_alloc on the old index return BadHandle, and a handle to the device sent before the quarantine arrives as 0. Keep the budget_usage and exhaustive-search checks as they are. P1-1 still holds because S comes from the runs and dma_mapped, not from handles.
> 
> Model: if it has per-process handle tables, sweep them too, so the kernel and the model both give BadHandle. Without in-message handles, record only that gap in VALIDATION.md. If it has no handle tables, stay flag-only with NotPermitted and record the difference. K5bQuarantinedDeviceUsable still applies either way.
> 
> Spec: when the docs commit lands, I'll write this into KERNEL-SPEC R10 and Device, and into answer 173's residual. The rule text: a device that fails its reset has its object destroyed as R10 does, and its base stays flagged until reboot. Tell me when that commit is ready. Proceed.
